## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

82	    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled.   (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.
  - Still open per the Confluence page: exact Test-gate design (deploy-then-gate as proposed, or match SIT's gate-then-deploy exactly) and its scope (P0 suite only, or also bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse).

## Unresolved Dependencies
Do not hard-code assumptions for the following — ask the user before implementing:
- Product copy ownership: Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 (TBD).
- Translation trigger workflow with TransPerfect (TBD).

- **Omneo guest record creation timing:** When to create an Omneo record for a guest (at newsletter sign-up, at back-in-stock capture, at checkout, or only at order completion) is under legal/SFCC best-practice review. SFCC best practice is order completion only. Do not create Omneo records for guests at any earlier point until confirmed. Note: CRM-012–015 are signed off but Tony Tilbrook (early creation) and Izzy Coxon (order-completion only) currently disagree on the timing — treat as Open until reconciled.

Confirm with Tell No Lies before doing SFCC data-layer work specifically for Optimizely.

Confirm which sheet is authoritative before relying on Einstein for cart/recommendation surfaces.

# PRD – Product Detail Page (PDP)

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Product, Catalogue and PDP" (PRD), "Cart & Inventory" (CAI), "Payments" (PAY), "Returns and Refunds" (RRC), "Customers, Account, CRM Sync" (CRM), "Order Management" (OM). Last updated: 2026-06-19.*

---

## 1. Page Structure

- Breadcrumb navigation displayed on all PDP pages (PRD-001, confirmed)
- Style code (SKU) displayed on PDP (PRD-007, confirmed)
- Key supporting information in expandable accordions: **Details, Size & Fit, Care, Shipping & Free Returns** (region-specific content) (PRD-008, confirmed)

---

## 2. Product Data

- Product name, price, sizes, and colour swatches sourced from the **Product API** (fed from AP21, but AP21 may not be the sole source in future — do not hard-code AP21 as the only data provider). Colour swatch assets do not live in AP21 — only colour names (PRD-002, confirmed — requirement updated for clarity 05.05)
- Style code (SKU) from product data (PRD-007, confirmed)
- "Also available in" / "Only available in" colour swatches; selecting a colour updates the page content and URL (PRD-004, confirmed). Hover-to-preview swatch behaviour (colour updates on rollover without click) is a **custom build, not OOTB, and not scoped for go-live** — see Open Items (PRD-004)
- *Open: product copy ownership (description, editorial text) — Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 is TBD (see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies")*

---

## 3. Product Badges & Tags (PRD-005 – PRD-006, confirmed)

- Products can carry one or more badges: **Campaign, Runway, Exclusive, Online Exclusive, VIC Exclusive** — badge *assignment* on applicable products is confirmed (PRD-005)
- Multiple badges per product are supported; a defined display priority/hierarchy applies when more than one badge is present
- Badge creation must not require a code deployment (PRD-005, comment: "ideally the creation of these badges would not require a code change")
- **Badges are clickable** and navigate the customer to a PLP view filtered to products in that badge category (PRD-005, confirmed — workbook updated 2026-06-19: "captured in requirement"). See also plp.md §2.6.
- *Design caveat: badges not yet present in PLP designs ("Missing badges in PLP") (PRD-005)*

---

## 4. Product States (PRD-010 – PRD-017, confirmed)

- **Coming Soon** — product is displayed on PDP before stock is added or purchase is enabled
- **Back in Soon** — product has sold out but will restock imminently (re-cut)
- **Unavailable (size-level)** — triggers the Notify Me flow for the affected size variant
- OOS sizes visually greyed out/disabled; Add to Bag is suppressed for that size variant (PRD-014)
- All product states (Coming Soon, Back in Soon, Unavailable) must comply with **Google Merchant Centre** feed rules — ineligible-state products must not surface in product feeds (PRD-017)
- Low-stock indicator at size level: displays **"LOW"** label — purely visual, does not alter CTA behaviour or block add-to-bag (PRD-012; also PRD-030 from CAI)

---

## 5. Pricing Display

- Display price in storefront currency (AUD, USD, GBP, EUR)
- Sale pricing: was/now format (PRD-003, confirmed — subject to designs). If price changes again after being put on sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042, confirmed)
- Tax label per storefront: GST (AU), VAT (UK/EU), Tax (US) (PAY, confirmed)
- **Duties and taxes information** displayed country-specifically on PDP (PRD-013, confirmed)
- **DDP/DDU messaging** displayed on PDP per applicable countries (PAY-059, confirmed)
- Max configurable purchase quantity enforced per customer group (PRD-011, confirmed)
- *Open: HK/ME/US Intl/EU Intl pricing display — Global-e pricing via SFCC price books is defined and REG-041 is confirmed (REG-040 retired). Sign-off of the full mechanism (PRC-34..PRC-43) is still pending; do not implement until confirmed.*

---

## 6. Availability & Add to Bag

*Buffer stock rules apply on PDP. See [cart.md](cart.md) section 5 for the full buffer stock system.*

- Per-size availability shown (ADD TO BAG / OUT OF STOCK / low-stock "LOW" indicator)
- **ADD TO BAG** shown when quantity is above buffer threshold
- **OUT OF STOCK** shown when quantity is at or below buffer threshold (back-in-stock capture presented)
- Low-stock indicator at size level — no quantity number shown — displays "LOW" label
- **Max 3 units per SKU** (same size + colour) enforced at add-to-cart (CAI-017, confirmed)
- **No soft reservation** at add-to-cart (CAI-032, confirmed)

---

## 7. Primary CTAs & Supporting Links (PRD-018 – PRD-022, confirmed)

- **Add to Bag** — primary CTA when in stock
- **Find in Boutique** — opens as a **slide-out** (not a modal) alongside Add to Bag (PRD-018)
- **Wishlist icon** — displayed alongside the primary CTA; size must be selected before wishlist save (PRD-019, PRD-020)
- Supporting links: **Unavailable** (opens slide-out notify me form), **Find My Size**, **Size Guide** (PRD-021)
- **Need Assistance** section: links to email, live chat (with availability hours caveat), and Contact Us (PRD-022). The "Contact Us" link is an external redirect to the Zendesk-hosted contact form — there is no embedded Zendesk integration in the storefront.

---

## 8. Find in Boutique (CAI-037 – CAI-042, PRD-028 – PRD-039)

The "Find in Boutique" CTA is shown on all eligible products. The feature opens as a **flyout/slide-out panel** (not a modal). All Find in Boutique requirements are now **confirmed** but carry a **Phase 2** design caveat (design not yet available — "Phase 2").

### Panel contents
- "Find in Boutique" CTA only displays for products where in-store stock checking is supported (PRD-028, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- At top of panel: product thumbnail, product name, selected colour, and price (PRD-029, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Size selector** pre-populated from the PDP selection; customer can change size within the panel (PRD-030, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- A **real-time inventory call** to NewStore via MuleSoft is made once a size is selected; the call refreshes when the customer selects a different size (CAI-038)
- **No auto-refresh** while the panel is open; boutique stock cached with configurable TTL (CAI-042)
- **Location search field** to filter boutique results (PRD-031, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **"Use My Location"** option triggers browser geolocation with explicit permission; handles failure case gracefully with inline message (PRD-032, PRD-033, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- **Maps integration** via Google Maps (via MRT API connection) for boutique directions (PRD-034, confirmed — Phase 2 design)
- Per-boutique results show: name, address, distance (if geolocation permitted), stock status (**In Stock / Low Stock – Contact Boutique to Confirm Availability / Out of Stock**), opening hours, contact details, current live open status (e.g. "OPEN – CLOSES AT 6:00PM"), map pin, and a view more button (PRD-035, confirmed). Opening hours and live open status are sourced from the **Google Business API** (with a manual override available in Business Manager) — distinct from the Google Maps integration used for the map pin and directions (TPI: Google Business API; Google Maps).
- **Get Directions** link per boutique result, opening the location in a maps application (PRD-036, confirmed)
- Configurable limit on number of boutique results displayed (PRD-039, confirmed)
- Display a clear message when no boutiques carry the selected size (CAI-041)
- **No buffer stock** applied to boutique inventory (CAI-040)
- Fully responsive across desktop, tablet, and mobile (PRD-037, confirmed)
- Enter key triggers search in the location field (PRD-038, confirmed)

---

## 9. Back-in-Stock Notifications / Stock Alert (OM-033 – OM-034, PRD-040 – PRD-049, confirmed)

Shown when product/size is OOS (Unavailable state):

- Stock alert CTA/link displayed on PDP when selected size is OOS (PRD-040)
- Opens as a slide-out with the stock alert sign-up form: product name, price, and product image thumbnail at top (PRD-041, PRD-042)
- **Multiple size selection supported** — customer selects which unavailable sizes to register for (PRD-043)
- Customer name and email captured as required fields; **pre-populated and editable for authenticated customers** (PRD-044)
- **Marketing opt-in/out checkbox** compliant with regional consent requirements, gated by Omneo consent management (PRD-045)
- Clear submission CTA to register the stock alert (PRD-046)
- Confirmation message shown within the slide-out on successful submission (PRD-047)
- Notifications sent **FIFO** to first configurable-N (default 30) customers when stock returns above buffer; if stock is still available after a configurable time window (default 30 minutes), the next batch of 30 receives the email (PRD-048)
- Stock replenishment signal flows from NewStore → MuleSoft → SFCC → email trigger (PRD-049)
- No loyalty tier prioritisation

---

## 10. Find My Size / Measmerize (PRD-050 – PRD-053)

The Measmerize widget is embedded on PDP and manages the Find My Size experience:

- Once Measmerize generates a recommendation, the system updates the CTA to display **"Recommended: Size X"** (PRD-050 — Measmerize widget manages behaviour)
- When the customer clicks "Recommended", the Measmerize widget handles navigation to the recommendation view — SFCC does not control this flow (PRD-051 removed as not applicable for SFCC)
- Whether the "Find My Size" link is shown/suppressed based on Measmerize data availability is managed by the Measmerize widget, not SFCC (PRD-052 removed as not applicable for SFCC)

---

## 11. Size Guide (PRD-053 – PRD-057, confirmed)

- Size guide opens as a **slide-out overlay** (not a modal) without navigating away from the PDP (PRD-053, confirmed)
- Size guide content is delivered via the **Measmerize overlay** (confirmed — VR/RT comment resolved 2026-06-19: "Yes is going to be a measmerize overlay"). The Contentful-managed size guide is shown as a fallback only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product.
- *SEO/LLM risk (acknowledged, not blocking): Measmerize is a third-party overlay; content rendered within it may not be indexable by search engines or LLMs. The decision to use Measmerize is made; this risk is noted for the team to monitor.*
- Size conversion tables appropriate to the selected product type (PRD-054)
- Size guide content managed as a **structured Contentful content type** per product type (Ready to Wear, Swim, Accessories, Belts, Jewellery, Men's, Denim, Hats, etc.) (PRD-055)
- **Measurement toggle: cm / inches** (PRD-056)
- Size guide content manageable without a code deployment — content managed via CMS (PRD-057, confirmed 2026-05-25)

---

## 12. EU Environmental Qualities / AGEC (PRD-009, confirmed)

- Environmental Qualities accordion rendered on EU storefronts (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`) only
- Data sourced from AP21
- **Only renders when data exists** — no placeholder or empty accordion shown

---

## 13. Content Modules

### As Seen / Seen on the Runway editorial module (PRD-023, confirmed)
- CMS-managed editorial imagery module per product or collection (per new designs, surfaced as "Seen on the Runway"). Confirmed subject to designs.

### Shop the Look (PRD-024, confirmed)
- "Shop the Look" module displayed on PDP; clicking a product navigates to its PDP
- Auto-hides if no related products are populated; excludes out-of-stock products

### Styling module (PRD-025, confirmed — requirement updated 06.05)
- Styling is part of the Shop the Look module (same thing) — treat as a Shop the Look variant, not a separate module.
- Applies to **dresses and jewellery**; must auto-hide if related content/products are not populated; must **not** display for kids, men's, or other accessories.

### You May Also Like (PRD-026, SPR-58, confirmed)
- "You May Also Like" carousel powered by SFCC Einstein; rules-based fallback at launch
- Note: design refers to this as "More Colourful x" — implement per final designs

### Recently Viewed (PRD-027, SPR-61, confirmed)
- "Recently Viewed" carousel / "See Full History"/"See All" button (design TBC) based on browsing session
- Session-based for guests; persists cross-session for logged-in customers

---

## 14. Product Imagery & Media (PRD-058 – PRD-070)

- Multiple images per product: front, back, detail, and model shots (PRD-058, confirmed)
- Thumbnail gallery navigation (PRD-059, confirmed)
- **Hover-to-zoom or click-to-expand lightbox** on primary image — desktop (PRD-060, confirmed)
- **Pinch-to-zoom and swipe-to-advance** gallery navigation — mobile and touch (PRD-061, confirmed)

- Images served in optimised format at appropriate resolutions per device breakpoint (PRD-063, confirmed)

- Optional **video content** (runway, model movement) as a tile in the image gallery; plays inline or expands to lightbox; multiple videos supported (e.g. studio, campaign, runway) (PRD-066, ready for sign off)
- Video autoplay configurable per video instance without a code deployment (PRD-068, ready for sign off)
- Flexible image presentation per page type (configurable background colour/treatment) without asset duplication (PRD-069, ready for sign off)
- Alt text required on all product images before a product can be published (PRD-070, ready for sign off)
- *Open: Video hosting platform — Vimeo is under consideration but not confirmed. Action open to confirm the best solution for smoothest FE experience (PRD-067). Note: the Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the media platform (embed URL stored in product data or CMS); this conflicts with PRD-067's challenging comment ("Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed") — treat as Open until the open action resolves.*

---

## 15. Non-Returnable / Final Sale Indicator (RRC-003, confirmed)

- Non-returnable / final sale indicator displayed on PDP for applicable products
- Applies to: gift cards, final sale items, and any SKU flagged non-returnable at SKU level
- Message copy is configurable

---

- Product catalogue feed provision through the existing feeds provider, **Feedonomics**. Feed supports product availability, stock positions, pricing, visibility, labels, and other metadata.
- Product feed volume is controllable at import via **job config** (07.05). OOTB product export is CSV; a non-CSV format is a **custom build**.

Perhaps this means having a state for products removed from store as well." (PRD-010)

7	### Template delivery scope (Storefront Templates sheet)

| SPR | Status | Requirement |

| SPR-54 | Confirmed | Merchandiser-configured search redirects — automatic navigation to a designated page when a redirect rule is triggered in Business Manager |
| SPR-55 | Confirmed | Product grid with columns that adapt responsively across desktop, tablet, and mobile |

content.thinking:
I'm uncovering something important about SFCC-83 — the base template actually uses an Einstein recommender called `viewed-recently-einstein` to power the "Recently Viewed" feature through the recommendations system, not a client-side session store. But the acceptance criteria specifies that guest sessions should only persist temporarily and clear when the browser closes, which seems to conflict with how the Einstein recommender works out of the box.

This creates a real architectural question: is the feature supposed to use the OOTB Einstein recommender (which relies on behavioral data and Einstein's user ID, but doesn't cleanly map to the stated persistence semantics), or does it need a custom implementation with session storage for guests and customer-profile persistence for authenticated users? The PRD mentions browsing history stored in browser session with cross-session persistence on login, and there's also SPR-58 which uses Einstein, so this is a significant fork in how we approach the estimate and what integration dependencies we're dealing with.

For authenticated cross-device persistence, the storage location is still unclear — SFCC doesn't natively support a recently-viewed list on the customer profile, so we'd need to either tie it to Einstein's user ID, create a custom SFCC customer attribute, or use Omneo, which ties back to the wishlist storage question. There's also a consent angle here: SFCC-83 noted that recently-viewed tracking continued even after rejecting cookies in AU/EU testing, suggesting it might be classified as functional rather than analytics, but gating Einstein behind Didomi consent creates a conflict. That's being split to SFCC-106, but the storage mechanism we choose will determine how we handle consent. Finally, the AC mentions a "See Full History" link that should navigate somewhere, but the destination is still undesigned.

The product tiles for recently-viewed are supposed to show image-only (no name or price per the PRD), but that means we can't reuse the standard `product-tile` or `ProductScroller` component — we need a custom image-only tile instead, which changes the shared component reuse assumptions.

Looking at the bigger picture, all six stories are marked Blocked with empty Sprint fields, which is a process red flag — we need to identify and clear the actual blockers before bringing them into a sprint. The DesignDependent label is scattered across stories, so we need clarity on which designs are already signed off versus still pending. Also, the header component (SFCC-52) already has a partial draft implementation from Squad A's Sprint 1 work, so the estimate needs to account for that existing code.

Before I lay it out: **all six share one live blocker** — `SFCC-240 "Spike: Figma-to-React Implementation Workflow"` (still *In Progress*). The earlier spike `SFCC-205` is Done. Here's the refinement briefing, structured around the angles you called out (desktop/mobile · behaviour · a11y · dependencies/blockers · data/SFCC config · estimation).

---

## Cross-cutting (raise once, applies to all six)

| # | Finding | Question for refinement |
|---|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | **All 6 are `Blocked` by `SFCC-240` (Figma→React workflow spike, *In Progress*).** It's the single gate on the whole batch. | What are SFCC-240's exit criteria and ETA? If it won't close before sprint start, none of these are sprint-ready. |

No `product-detail` page, `footer`, `product-tile`, `swatch-group`, `display-price`, `breadcrumb`, `drawer-menu`, `recommended-products`. | Each PDP/footer story carries a copy-first step (copy base → TS-convert → `tsc` → console.log verify → user test) per AGENTS.md before functional work. Footer specifically is still open on design. |

---

## SFCC-52 — Global Header UI (3 pts · Epic: Homepage & Nav · Blocked)

**Reality:** A draft header already exists (`overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`, self-labelled *"draft, unfinished"*) — two-row layout, Account/Saved/Bag as **text** buttons, a TEMP debug search input, mobile account/wishlist icons **commented out**, no drawer wired.

- **Scope split is unresolved in-ticket (Tim, 07-26):** AC 4–5 (bag count) arguably belong to Cart; AC 7–11 (hamburger drawer, drill-down) belong to Nav (`SFCC-97`, related). Close this before pointing — as written, AC overlaps two other stories.
- **⚠️ PRD contradiction — Wishlist/"Saved" in header?** Story AC lists desktop icons as *Search, Account, **Saved**, Bag*; the built header shows "Saved". But `homepage.md` HPC-018 records the confirmed header set as **Search / Account / Bag only** (per 23-Jun design review), while HPC-019/020 still describe wishlist-icon behaviour. Genuine doc tension — **confirm whether Saved/Wishlist is a header element** before we build it in or strip it out.
- **Behaviour:** AC says bag count updates "without full page reload" — the draft already does this via `useCurrentBasket`. Sticky-on-scroll confirmed; but **mobile unstick-on-scroll-up (Jacquemus-style) is a pending design per HPC-015** — in or out for this story?
- **Desktop vs mobile:** icons are text on desktop, icon-cluster on mobile — matches AC. Mega menu = `SFCC-96`, hamburger drawer = `SFCC-97` (both separate). Confirm this story is *shell + sticky + logo→home only*.
- **A11y:** icon-only buttons need `aria-label` (enforced by ast-grep); the account popover needs focus-trap/Esc/return-focus; announce bag-count changes. Confirm a11y is in the DoD, not deferred to Nav.
- **Estimation:** 3 is fair *if* it's shell-only and we reuse the draft — but the draft has debt (commented icons, TEMP search). Flag risk that "finish the draft properly + a11y" ≈ the same as fresh.

## SFCC-55 — Global Footer UI (3 pts · Epic: Homepage & Nav · Blocked)

- **⚠️ Source-of-truth contradiction:** AC #7 says a merchandiser defines footer links **"in SFCC"**, but PRD HPC-030/038 say the footer is **Contentful-managed**, and there's a dedicated `SFCC-117 "Global Footer — Contentful"`. Confirm: shell here consumes **placeholder** links now, structured for Contentful injection later — and fix AC#7's "SFCC" → "CMS."
- **Behaviour:** email input is an **explicit placeholder** (Omneo + first/last-name modal is `SFCC-99`, which this blocks). Rollover = underline on hover (added as AC 07-07). Confirm keyboard-focus state mirrors hover (a11y).

- **Region/currency selector:** AC puts a "region/currency indicator" in the bottom bar; HPC-026 says the selector appears in footer **on all storefronts except AU**. Is this story rendering the **interactive selector** or a **display-only indicator**? (Selector logic may be its own story.)

- **Blocker note:** design **not** signed off (Dani) — this is the actual thing keeping it Blocked beyond SFCC-240. This story **blocks** SFCC-99 and SFCC-117.
- **Estimation:** 3 reasonable for shell; low risk *if* design lands.

## SFCC-89 — PDP Static Product Information (3 pts · Epic: PDP · Blocked)

- **Hard data dependency:** **blocked by `SFCC-26 "Product Attributes – PDP"` (in Code Review).** The "Model is…" copy needs a **new SFCC product attribute** (comment 07-03: it was bundled in Magento's "size & fit"), and Style Code needs to be exposed. ## SFCC-91 — PDP Colour Swatches & Variation Selection (3 pts · Epic: PDP · Blocked) — **biggest technical unknown**

- **⚠️ The two "Swatch selection" ACs contradict each other:** one says colour change updates URL **without full page reload**; the next says it updates to a **new style code with a full page reload**. These describe two different data models:
  - Base `swatch-group` (OOTB) assumes colours are **variation attributes of one master** → in-page swap, no reload.
  - But real zimmermann.com models each colour as a **separate product / style code** (`lumi-sandal-lilac.html`) → full navigation, new URL, new SKU.

PRD-004 open item: *"colour swatch management and mapping — TBC (SPR-26)."*

Confirm the colour→index-image mapping mechanism exists in the test org. Single-colour → text label ("Colour: Bay Blue"), no swatch. Max ~7 colours (Dani, confirmed).

- **A11y:** swatches as a labelled radio-group (each has an accessible colour name), keyboard-selectable, selected state not conveyed by border alone.
- **Estimation:** **challenge the 3.** Under the separate-product model I'd expect 5–8 + likely a spike. Needs the data-model decision *first*.

- **⚠️ Duplicate stories exist:** SFCC-92 is marked **duplicated by `SFCC-293` (ATB/OOS by buffer threshold)** and **`SFCC-295` (low-stock indicator at size level)** — both cover the same buffer/low-stock ACs. Reconcile/close duplicates or you'll double-point and double-build.

Buffer thresholds come from **`SFCC-239` (Buffer Stock Threshold Config, In Refinement)**. Coming Soon/all-sizes-unavailable split to **`SFCC-150`**. - **Behaviour:** interim ATB routes to **OOTB SFCC cart** (real cart is a later story) — fine, confirm acceptable for demo. One-size product → no selector, single size shown. Buffer logic (stock > buffer = selectable) needs buffer config in test env.
- **Desktop vs mobile:** size selector as pills/list; touch target sizing (a11y ≥ 44px).
- **A11y:** radio-group semantics, disabled sizes still announced as unavailable, error text linked via `aria-describedby`.
- **Estimation:** 5 is plausible for the "base version" **only after** de-dupe and the split decision — otherwise scope is ambiguous.

## SFCC-83 — Recently Viewed UI Component (Shared) (3 pts · Epic: Search & Recommendations · Blocked) — **architecture fork**

- **⚠️ Storage model doesn't match OOTB.** Base template's "Recently Viewed" is an **Einstein recommender** (`'viewed-recently-einstein'`, used on Cart/PDP via `RecommendedProducts`). But the AC requires **guest = session-only, cleared on browser close** and **auth = cross-session, cross-device, restored on login from the account**. Einstein's behavioural recommender doesn't cleanly give those semantics.
  - **Where does authenticated cross-device history persist?** SFCC has no native "recently viewed" list on the customer profile → options are Einstein usid, a **custom SFCC customer attribute**, or **Omneo**. This ties directly to the open **wishlist SFCC-vs-Omneo** decision. **This choice defines the estimate.**

- **Estimation:** **challenge the 3.** With a custom store + authenticated cross-device persistence + a custom tile, I'd expect 5+ and possibly a spike on the persistence backend.

what is the difference between colour swatch vs. new style code?

content.thinking:
I'm looking at the two contradicting acceptance criteria from SFCC-91 for swatch selection — one labeled "Colour variation" that expects a URL update without a full page reload, and another labeled "New Style Code" that expects a URL update with a new style code and a full page reload. The distinction seems to hinge on whether selecting a colour swatch triggers just a variation change or an entirely new style code, which determines the reload behavior.

This gets at a fundamental SFCC data modeling question: whether colour is modeled as a variation attribute within a single master product (where clicking a swatch just changes the variant), or whether each colour is actually a separate master product with its own style code (where clicking a swatch navigates to a different product entirely, hence the full reload). A colour swatch is just the UI element, but whether clicking it loads a new style code hinges on the data model — if each colour is a separate product (Model B), you get a new URL and full reload; if it's a variation (Model A), you stay on the same page with JS swapping the details. The team's caught between these two approaches, and the choice determines whether to use OOTB swatch-group functionality or build something custom. Model A is cheaper and smoother UX-wise but requires the catalogue to structure colours as variants on a master product, whereas Model B treats each colour as its own product with its own identity.

There's a third path worth considering: keep colours as separate products but use client-side navigation instead of a hard reload, so the URL and style code change without the browser refreshing the whole page. That could satisfy both bullets — new style code and new URL, but with the perceived performance and UX benefits of a soft transition.

Looking back at the PRD, there's something important: PRD-062 explicitly states the gallery updates when a colour swatch is selected without a full page reload. That's Model A behaviour and it's already confirmed in the spec. But the Lumi Sandal example uses per-colour URLs, which suggests Model B. There's a tension here between what the PRD says should happen and what the reference example shows.

The real issue is that SFCC-91's acceptance criteria calls for "new style code + full reload" (Model B), while PRD-062 says no reload (Model A). So I need to lay out both models clearly, show which one matches the actual site and the PRD, and then surface this contradiction as something to resolve in the meeting. A comparison table would help make this concrete for the team.

content.text:
Good question — the two AC bullets aren't just worded differently, they describe **two different catalogue data models**, and "style code" is the tell.

**Quick definitions**
- **Colour swatch** = the UI element (the clickable thumbnail for each colour).
- **Style code** = the product's *identity* in SFCC (the SKU / product ID that the PDP URL resolves to).

The question the AC never settles: **when you click another colour, are you staying on the same product or navigating to a different one?** That depends on how colours are modelled.

| | **Model A — colour as a variation** | **Model B — colour as its own product** |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC structure | One master product; colour + size are variation attributes | Each colour is a **separate product with its own style code** |
| Clicking a swatch | Swaps the variant *within the same product* | **Navigates to a different product page** |
| URL | Same page, e.g. `?color=lilac` | New URL, e.g. `…/lumi-sandal-lilac` → `…/lumi-sandal-black` |
| Style code | Unchanged | **Changes** (new SKU) |
| Reload | **No reload** (JS swap) | New product load |
| Maps to AC bullet | "Colour variation… **without full page reload**" | "**New Style Code**… full page reload" |
| Build | OOTB base `swatch-group` — cheap (~3) | Custom: colour-group + sibling links + navigation (~5–8 + spike) |
| SEO | One URL for all colours | Each colour independently indexable (better) |

So they're the same click producing **opposite outcomes** — that's the contradiction. It can't be both; the team has to pick the model.

**Which is real?** The live site points to **Model B** — each colour is its own URL (`lumi-sandal-lilac.html`), and that usually mirrors the AP21/ERP reality where each colourway is a distinct style code. That's also why the base `swatch-group` won't work as-is and why I flagged the estimate risk.

**But there's a PRD tension too:** `pdp.md` **PRD-062 (confirmed)** says *"gallery updates … when a colour swatch is selected, **without a full page reload**"* — i.e. Model A behaviour, contradicting the "new style code + reload" bullet.

**Likely reconciliation to propose in the room:** colours *are* separate products/style codes (Model B), but the swatch does a **client-side (SPA) route change** — new URL + new style code, but **no hard browser reload**. That satisfies PRD-062's "no reload," keeps SEO-friendly per-colour URLs, and protects the LCP budget. If that's the intent, the AC should be rewritten as one bullet, not two.

**Ask:** "Are colourways separate style codes or variation attributes — and if separate, do we want a hard reload or a soft client-side transition?" That one answer resolves the AC *and* locks the estimate.

content.thinking:
I'm working through a concrete implementation strategy for Model B on the PWA Kit—where color variants are treated as separate products with smooth client-side navigation. I need to ground this in how the commerce-sdk-react and SFCC codebase actually work to give a solid architectural blueprint.

The core challenge is that SFCC doesn't natively group separate products by color the way it does with variation attributes, so I need to figure out the right linking mechanism. I'm evaluating options like product sets, custom attributes, or a catalog-level grouping strategy to connect these color siblings so the PDP can render swatches and navigate between them seamlessly.

The cleanest approach is adding a custom `c_colourGroupId` attribute to each product that shares a base style code, then querying all products in that group via the Shopper Search API with a refinement filter. Each product would also carry its own color name and swatch image so the UI can render the full color palette.

I'm weighing the trade-offs between different retrieval methods: searching by the grouping attribute is simple and gets all siblings in one call, but requires the search index to expose that custom attribute as a refinement. Alternatively, I could denormalize the sibling list directly onto each product as a JSON array of color variants—this eliminates the second request and search-index dependency, making it faster for page load, though it means the data needs to stay in sync through a feed or job.

Given Zimmermann's existing AP21 feed pipeline, denormalizing the sibling array is the most practical approach for performance. The PDP's product response would include either the group ID or the full sibling array, and the frontend renders swatches from that data.

For navigation, since each color is a separate product, clicking a swatch needs to route to that sibling's PDP URL using client-side SPA navigation.

React Query handles refetching the new product data, and if it's prefetched, the transition is seamless. Each color variant gets its own canonical, crawlable URL with real anchor tags for SEO and progressive enhancement—so crawlers follow the links and users can open swatches in new tabs. Prefetching the sibling product on hover makes the soft navigation instant and protects LCP. The currently viewed product's swatch gets marked as selected with the appropriate ARIA attribute.

To build these URLs, I'm using the app's `productUrlBuilder` utility with each sibling's product ID to generate the proper SEO path. Since each color is a separate product, each one still has its own size variants underneath—the color products are masters over their size attributes.

For the component structure, the PDP page container fetches both the product data and the color group (either denormalized or via a dedicated hook), then passes that down to a presentational component that handles rendering the color swatches.

The swatch component itself stays simple and prop-driven—it receives an array of swatch objects with product IDs, color names, image URLs, and selection state, then renders them as clickable anchors. A custom hook encapsulates the logic for fetching sibling products in the color group and handles any prefetching, keeping the data-fetching concerns separate from the UI layer.

For Model B, I'm treating the color swatch group as its own distinct component rather than trying to reuse the base swatch-group, since the semantics are different—this avoids conflating variation attributes with cross-product grouping logic. Single colour just shows a text label instead of swatches, and colours without index images get filtered out per the requirements. I need to handle the layout wrapping for groups up to seven swatches, and while out-of-stock colours could be flagged as a question, I'll keep them visible since availability is managed at the size level on the target PDP. Each sibling product has its own price, so the swatch component doesn't need to handle pricing.

For implementation, I'm building sibling URLs with locale and site prefixes using the multi-site utility, and I'm denormalizing the sibling list to avoid extra requests and keep the LCP optimal—if I do need search-based data, that request runs in parallel without blocking the first paint. I'll add prefetching on hover or intersection, use soft navigation instead of hard reloads, and render real anchor tags to each sibling's canonical URL so search engines can crawl them properly. I'll structure the answer with a component responsibility breakdown, show the data-source decision between denormalized and search options, walk through the click and navigation flow, and touch on SEO, accessibility, and performance considerations — all grounded in the repo's conventions and Tier system. Now I'm mapping out the full proposal: the data model and SFCC configuration needed (grouping attribute, swatch imagery, colour naming), then deciding between a denormalised sibling list versus search-by-group. The frontend architecture breaks down into the page container, a custom hook for colour grouping, and the swatch component itself, each with clear ownership and tier assignments. The swatch acts as a real anchor triggering soft navigation with prefetch via react-router and React Query, keeping the experience instant without hard reloads. I'll also cover SEO, accessibility, performance, and edge cases, then tie it back to the story with prerequisites, estimation, and any spikes needed.

For the data model specifically, denormalised is the right call here—storing the colour group directly on the product record and fetching it in the same `getProduct` call avoids a second network request that would block LCP. Luxury brands like Zimmermann have tight performance budgets, and swatches sit above the fold as part of the product identity, so any waterfall risk is unacceptable. The pipeline cost is manageable since they already have a feed system in place (AP21 → Feedonomics), and colour grouping is stable data that doesn't churn. content.text:
Cleanly, in PWA-Kit terms, Model B comes down to one principle:

> **Externalise *colour* to sibling products; keep *size* as an OOTB variation attribute; move between colours with a client-side (soft) route change, not a hard reload.**

That split is what keeps it clean — you're not fighting the framework's variation model, you're only adding a cross-product *grouping* layer on top of it. Size, price, gallery, add-to-bag all stay standard.

### 1. Data / SFCC config (the prerequisite)

Each colour product needs three things on its record:

| Field | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `c_colourGroupId` | Shared key linking sibling colourways (e.g. the style root `lumi-sandal`) |
| `c_colourName` | Accessible label for the swatch ("Bay Blue") |
| index/swatch image | The representative image per colour (PRD-004) |

**Two ways to fetch the group — pick one:**

| Option | How | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Denormalised (recommended)** | Store the sibling list as a JSON custom attr on the product, returned by the *same* `useProduct` call | **No second request → best for LCP**; no search-index dependency. Cost: a feed/job must populate it (Zimmermann already has AP21 → Feedonomics pipeline) |
| **B. Search-by-group** | `useProductSearch` refined on `c_colourGroupId` | No pipeline work, but a second (parallel) call + search-index latency, and the attr must be a searchable refinement |

Recommend **A** — swatches are part of the product identity and should render on first paint without a waterfall.

### 2. Front-end architecture (tight footprint — 1 hook + 1 component)

| Piece | Path | Responsibility | Tier / note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Container | `pages/product-detail/` | Calls `useProduct`; reads the colour group; passes swatch view-models down | Squad A |
| Hook | `hooks/useColourGroup.ts` | Maps group → `{productId, colourName, swatchImageUrl, href, isSelected}[]`; filters colours with no index image; builds locale-aware URLs; prefetches siblings | new, Zimmermann-authored |
| Component | `components/colourSwatchGroup/` | **Presentational only** — renders anchors, selected state, single-colour label | new (not a `swatch-group` override — different semantics) |

Keep data-fetching in the container (per `components.md`); the swatch component just receives props → Storybook-able, testable.

### 3. The "clean" navigation pattern

Each swatch is a **real `<a href>` to the sibling's canonical URL**, with JS intercepting the click for a **soft SPA navigation** (react-router via the existing `use-navigation` hook — Tier 1, call it, don't modify):

```tsx
// illustrative — colourSwatchGroup renders links, not buttons
<Link
  to={swatch.href}                         // real, crawlable URL
  aria-label={swatch.colourName}           // image-only swatch needs this
  aria-current={swatch.isSelected ? 'page' : undefined}
  onMouseEnter={() => prefetch(swatch.productId)}  // instant on click
>
  <Image src={swatch.swatchImageUrl} alt={swatch.colourName} />
</Link>
```

- **New URL + new style code, no hard reload** → satisfies the "new style code" bullet *and* PRD-062's "without full page reload." commerce-sdk-react's React Query refetches the sibling; prefetch-on-hover makes it feel instant → protects the LCP budget.
- Real anchor = SEO-crawlable per-colour URLs + cmd/click / open-in-new-tab work for free (progressive enhancement).

### 4. Cross-cutting

| Angle | Approach |
|---|---|
| **A11y** | Treat as a **list of links** (navigation), not a radio-group — native focus/Enter, accessible name = colour, current = `aria-current="page"` |
| **SEO** | Each colour canonical to its own URL; SEO/hreflang already handled per product |
| **Perf** | Denormalised group (no waterfall) + prefetch + soft-nav; swatches don't block first paint if search-based (skeleton) |
| **Edge cases** | 1 colour → text label, no swatches · colour w/o index image → excluded (AC) · ≤7 wrap · OOS colour still shown (availability handled at size level on target PDP — *confirm*) |
| **Testing** | Vitest on `useColourGroup` (mapping/filter/URL) · Storybook `Default/SingleColour/SevenColours/WithUnavailable` · Playwright: click → URL+style-code change, no full reload, selected state |

### What this means for SFCC-91
- **Blocked on catalogue config** (`c_colourGroupId` + swatch image + colour name) — ties to SFCC-26 and the still-open "colour mapping exercise" (PRD-004). This must land in the test org first.
- **Re-point:** with a custom hook + component + the nav/prefetch work, this is realistically **5–8, not 3** — and I'd run a **half-day spike** to confirm the grouping attribute + soft-nav prefetch behaviour before committing the estimate.

The business has clarified the colour model question I had earlier — SFCC uses a standard three-level hierarchy where colour variants of the same product are naturally modelled as variation groups within a master product, each holding colour-specific attributes and images alongside their individual SKU variants for different sizes.

The key new piece is SFCC-708, which introduces a custom `Related Colours` attribute that merchandisers populate with comma-separated style codes to link entirely separate master products that aren't natural variants of each other — this is the cross-product colour linking I was looking for. The behaviour mirrors SFCC-91: clicking a colour swatch navigates to the new style code with a full page reload. Dani's latest comment adds important nuances: swatches only display if the related colour has stock available, and within the expanded image gallery, colour swatches trigger image changes on hover without leaving the popup.

So the implementation is actually a hybrid approach — natural colour variants stay within a master using standard variation groups with no reload, while cross-product colours use the `Related Colours` attribute to navigate between separate masters. So both scenarios are valid but they're fundamentally different interactions — variation swatches within the same master product trigger an in-page swap, while related colour swatches navigate to a different product entirely with a full reload and new style code. This means the PDP needs to handle both swatch types simultaneously, which adds complexity. There are also specific rendering rules: the order of style codes determines swatch display order, invalid codes don't error at save but fail silently at render, and related colours that aren't yet in stock shouldn't display their swatches at all. Now I'm looking at how the draft component stories fit into this.

The new approach is shifting toward component-first architecture under a separate epic for PWA Kit Components — breaking down the PDP into atomic, reusable pieces like the hero, add-to-bag, and size-selector with clean prop interfaces and explicit accessibility requirements. But this creates a critical overlap: the new component stories are blocking the older page-level PDP story, which suggests there's duplication between the two approaches that needs to be resolved. So the key refinement is reconciling SFCC-92 as an integration umbrella against these new component-level stories, especially since SFCC-648 and SFCC-650 both depend on SFCC-150 (the states story that's now Ready For Review). I'm also seeing the dual-epic structure take shape: SFCC-2 handles the atomic components themselves (size selector, add-to-bag, hero), while SFCC-5 owns the page-level integration stories that compose them together.

The architecture is actually clean—BM config (SFCC-4) feeds into atomic components (SFCC-2), which then feed into page assembly (SFCC-5)—but I need to be explicit about which stories own which responsibilities, otherwise we'll end up building the same thing twice. The tension is between SFCC-648 as a component story versus SFCC-92 as a page story, and I need to clarify which one the dev should actually implement.

I'm also noticing that none of these stories have story point estimates yet, and only SFCC-268 and SFCC-434 are assigned to an active sprint (SFCC Sprint 3, which runs through August 24th). The rest are unscheduled, so there's a planning gap here. I'm checking the codebase to understand the existing wishlist implementation — the base retail-react-app already has wishlist functionality built in with hooks and account pages, and SFCC-434 is leveraging that out-of-the-box behavior rather than building something custom.

There's a design tension I need to flag: the requirements (CRM-127/128) specify one size per product, but the acceptance criteria says one size per color variant, and the current live site enforces one size per product. Jasmijn noted this discrepancy and suggested logging an enhancement, with Emma proposing to capture the confirmation message behavior as a separate ticket.

For the wishlist implementation itself, the OOTB SFCC customer product lists store variant SKUs, so saving at the size level works fine—but there's a UX complication around how the wishlist icon should reflect color and size changes.

The icon state logic needs custom handling to check if any size of the current color variant is already wishlisted and prevent adding duplicates. There's also a requirement that size must be selected before saving to wishlist, and guest users need to go through the login flow. The bigger open question is whether the wishlist will be hosted in SFCC or Omneo—Mani apparently confirmed OOTB SFCC behavior, so it looks like we're going with SFCC-hosted for launch, which should resolve that decision point.

I'm also tracking the status shifts on related tickets: SFCC-91 and SFCC-92 have moved out of blocked (SFCC-91 is now ready for development, SFCC-89 is in progress), and SFCC-132 for badges is approved but still blocked by SFCC-225 and SFCC-236, which are both in review.

The badges story itself has significant complexity I need to account for: it depends on the BM config for badge creation and priority rules, requires PLP filtering capability for clickable badges, and includes locale-specific labels plus region and customer-group gating (like the VIC Exclusive badge tied to CRM). This clarifies that badges are their own distinct story rather than just part of the description work.

Now looking at SFCC-236, the shared product card component that's blocking the Recently Viewed full history page. The full-history tiles are supposed to match PLP tile behavior, but that seems to conflict with what I found earlier about the Recently Viewed rail showing image-only tiles without name or price.

So there are actually two different tile treatments here: the rail uses image-only tiles, while the full history page displays full product cards matching the PLP style. SFCC-84 depends on SFCC-83 for the data source, SFCC-236 for the card component, and SFCC-80 for the PLP tile reference. The persistence question still lingers about where the full history data originates, and there was some discussion about Contentful that's since been clarified — product images stay in SFCC, not Contentful. Design has provided reference images for this.

Now I'm looking at the component stories (648, 650, 723) which are still in draft and work-in-progress. Jasmijn is asking for early feedback, so I should review these as a senior frontend lead would: checking if the component boundaries are well-defined, if the composition is clean, whether the acceptance criteria are testable, spotting any gaps, and verifying alignment with repo conventions like container/presentational patterns, Chakra-first approach, Storybook setup, and accessibility standards. I'm noticing a discrepancy too — the component stories reference WCAG 2.1 AA as the minimum, but the project documentation targets WCAG 2.2 AA, so that's something to flag.

For SFCC-650 specifically, there's been a resolution to the earlier contradiction about the add-to-bag button's disabled state. The new ACs clarify it as: the button displays as disabled, and when a user attempts interaction, a "Size required" inline message appears. Though there's a technical detail here — a disabled button in HTML can't actually receive click events, so the implementation approach needs to be thought through carefully.

Looking at the accessibility requirements across the ACs, there's a subtle tension: AC#1 calls for a disabled state, AC#2 expects clicking to surface a message (which requires the button to be focusable and interactive), and AC#10 requires the unavailable state to be announced to screen readers. The cleanest pattern here would be using `aria-disabled` instead of the native `disabled` attribute — that way the button remains focusable, can intercept clicks to show the message, and screen readers can properly announce its unavailable state. This resolves the latent contradiction across the three ACs.

Looking at the scope breakdown, C-650 confirms that the add-to-bag component owns the actual cart API integration — unlike the older SFCC-92 which used the out-of-the-box cart. The component handles size validation, stock awareness via props, the cart API call itself, plus loading and error states. SFCC-648 (the size-selector) is well-specified with 21 ACs covering keyboard navigation, aria labels that include stock status, live region announcements for errors, and proper handling of single-size products.

The size-selector introduces four stock states (in stock, low stock, out of stock, notify me) plus a "recommended" indicator tied to Measmerize data. There's a gap though — the spec treats "recommended" as a prop but doesn't clarify how the size-selector receives that data from the Measmerize widget, which is a third-party overlay. That's an integration question that needs answering. SFCC-723 (the pdp/hero component) is the layout orchestrator that composes the gallery and product details together.

Now looking at the hero component's structure — it handles desktop/mobile layouts (gallery left/content right on desktop, stacked on mobile) with a carousel showing a 2x2 grid, video controls, and a dot indicator. A few things to clarify: the component references "pdp/product-content" as a child but that's not in this batch, so that's a dependency to track. The image gallery itself seems custom-built with the 2x2 grid, video support, and View Gallery overlay — that's not coming from the base image-gallery component, which means significant scope there. And the View Gallery overlay that opens an expanded gallery popup needs to be defined somewhere.

The prop contract for how children get passed in is also unclear — the acceptance criteria mentions accepting child components as composed instances (carousel, product-content, colour picker, size selector, add-to-bag, drawer triggers), but I need to confirm whether these are named slots or a single children prop. That's a lot of slots to coordinate. The component is marked high priority under epic SFCC-2 with no estimate yet, and I'm starting to see how the existing codebase has image-gallery, product-view, and swatch-group components, but the Zimmerm—

Actually, the Zimmermann design has a custom carousel (2x2 grid, video support, dot navigation, View Gallery overlay) that the base image-gallery doesn't support, so this hero plus gallery combination is going to be substantial custom work. What's also becoming clear is that the team has shifted to a component-first atomic decomposition under epic SFCC-2, which will then be composed into pages under epic SFCC-5. That's the right direction and matches the repo's conventions, but the older page-level stories (SFCC-89/91/92) are overlapping with these new component stories, and I need to reconcile them so we're not building the same thing twice — that's really the key issue for this refinement. None of these are estimated yet, and only two (268, 434) are already in progress.

Looking at the readiness: two stories are in Sprint 3 but unestimated, three drafts (648/650/723) are still work-in-progress and not ready to estimate until we sort out the reconciliation and make a couple of decisions. The catalogue configs (25, 268, 708) are backend and Business Manager configuration work with clear tech design. The max quantity UI story (196) has solid tech design now after being split. A couple of stories are blocked — 132 is waiting on 225, and 84 is waiting on 236.

For the analysis itself, I should lead with the 2-3 headline findings: the component-first versus page-level reconciliation, the colour model now resolved through stories 25 and 708, the WCAG version question, and the fact that we have unestimated work already in the sprint. Then I'll group the analysis by the three draft component stories first.

I'm planning to structure this with cross-cutting findings up front, then per-story mini-tables that focus on behaviour, desktop-mobile differences, accessibility, dependencies, and estimation. I'll highlight the contradictions and decisions that need attention. Let me map out the dependencies and epics to make the relationships clear. The remaining tasks in the PDP epic are blocked on the size and add-to-bag components, which depend on the size-selector and add-to-bag PWA Kit pieces. The colour swatch feature chains together the variation model, related colours attribute, and the UI component. There are also several supporting features like max quantity configuration, wishlist, and notification states that feed into these core flows, plus search recommendations work queued up. Recently viewed needs the full history view plus product card display and consent handling. For estimation, the size selector looks solid at around 5 points given all the states and keyboard navigation, add-to-bag is probably 3 to 5 depending on cart API complexity, but the hero banner is tricky — if it includes a custom carousel with 2x2 grid, video, and gallery view, that could balloon to 8 or more and might need to be split out separately.

Looking at the remaining tickets: the variation model is mostly configuration work around 3 to 5 points, max quantity config is small at 2 to 3, the UI for max quantity tracking is medium at 3 to 5, wishlist needs custom icon state logic on top of OOTB at 5, badges are medium-high at 5 but blocked by other work, related colors is straightforward config and rendering at 3, and the full history page reuses the card component at 3 but also blocked. I'll frame these as suggested points for discussion rather than definitive.

There are a few key tensions worth surfacing: the component-first approach in epic 2 overlaps with page-level work in epic 5, with SFCC-648 and 650 potentially blocking SFCC-92, and SFCC-293 and 295 look like duplicates—we should reconcile these so we're not building the same thing twice, maybe reframing SFCC-92 as integration or closing it out. On the color side, we've resolved the model but now have two paths: SFCC-25 handles variation groups that stay in the master without reloading, while SFCC-708 handles related colors across products with a new style code and reload. SFCC-91 needs to support both swatch types on a single PDP with gallery rollover preview, so the acceptance criteria should split by scenario to clarify what each one handles.

We also need to bump the WCAG standard from 2.1 AA to 2.2 AA to match the project baseline. The add-to-bag button has a conflict between "disabled" and "click shows message" plus "announced"—switching to aria-disabled resolves that. And there's an unresolved gap between the wishlist requirement of one size per product versus the AC calling for one size per color variant, plus the UX around resetting the wishlist icon on size change and the confirmation message that's moving to SFCC-710. The wishlist story assumes SFCC out-of-the-box, which Mani confirmed, but the Omneo integration is still an open question.

For max quantity, we're splitting the per-group and SKU logic into an enhancement (SFCC-703) and keeping a global default here, though we'll need to confirm the precedence order later—SKU should win over group which wins over default. Badges got removed from this story's scope and are now their own ticket (SFCC-225), but they'll need work across PLP and product cards with region and locale gating. There are two unestimated stories already in Sprint 3 (268 and 434). The recently viewed storage backend is still unresolved from an earlier story and affects another one downstream. Dani just added a comment today about gallery rollover preview behavior and stock-gated functionality that needs to be factored in.

The swatch visibility piece is new and might not be in the acceptance criteria yet—I should flag that. SFCC-708 also has some style code handling that skips validation at save time and just skips invalid code at render time, which gives us clear testable criteria. Looking at the actual codebase, the base has an image gallery, product view, swatch group, wishlist, and product tile components, but no custom carousel and no footer or PDP page overrides yet. The OOTB wishlist already exists, but the base image gallery doesn't have the custom carousel we need, and the swatch group only handles variation attributes—it won't work for cross-product related colors.

I have enough context from the component listing and account page structure to move forward without more tool calls. I'm confident the base template ships with customer product-list APIs and a wishlist account page. I'll structure the analysis with the epic architecture shift as the headline and work from there.

I'm planning to organize this as cross-cutting decisions, then group the draft stories separately from the approved ones, include a table of suggested story points to discuss, and wrap with action items. I'll use tables per story with angle and question columns, marking key decisions with warning indicators.

Now I'm diving into the hero story details—

it references the parent epic and has a dependency on product content that's outside this batch. The gallery carousel needs custom functionality beyond the base component (2x2 grid, video controls, dot indicators, overlay), so I should flag whether that warrants its own story. The focus order and accessibility standards look solid, but I need to clarify where the "recommended" state comes from (Measmerize integration) and who provides the stock status prop upstream.

For the size selector story, it's well-documented overall, but there's coupling between the size-selector and add-to-bag error states that needs attention—the error state gets triggered externally, and I should note the mobile variant and one-size label handling.

Now looking at the add-to-bag component: the cart API is in scope, but there's a contradiction between disabled and aria-disabled that needs resolving. The success state is unclear—is it a toast, mini-cart update, or does it open the mini-bag? That ties into the header bag count and the fly-to-bag animation. There's also sibling coupling through the hero composition since it pulls size state and stock from the size-selector. I need to confirm the success UX flow and whether max quantity is handled separately.…

content.text:
Big deltas since we last looked — and they're mostly good news. Two of the ambiguities I flagged in the earlier batch have now been **answered by the business**, and the team has clearly shifted to a **component-first decomposition**. That shift is the single most important thing to get straight in this refinement, because it overlaps the older page-level PDP stories.

Here's the full pre-read.

## The headline: two parallel decompositions now exist for the same PDP

| Epic | Approach | Stories in this batch |
|---|---|---|
| **SFCC-2 PWA Kit Components** (new) | Atomic, reusable, design-system-sourced components, props-only | SFCC-723 `pdp/hero`, SFCC-650 `pdp/add-to-bag`, SFCC-648 `pdp/size-selector` |
| **SFCC-5 PDP** | Page-level UI stories | SFCC-89 static, SFCC-91 colour, **SFCC-92 size+ATB**, SFCC-196 max-qty, SFCC-434 wishlist, SFCC-132 badges |
| **SFCC-4 Product Catalogue** | BM / catalogue config | SFCC-25 variation model, SFCC-268 max-qty config, SFCC-708 related colours |
| **SFCC-7 Search & Recs** | | SFCC-84 Recently Viewed – full history |

**⚠️ #1 reconciliation to resolve:** SFCC-648 + SFCC-650 both **`block` SFCC-92** — i.e. they *are* the decomposition of the old "Size Selection & Add to Bag" story. Combined with the duplicates I flagged last time (SFCC-293/295) and the states story (SFCC-150), SFCC-92 is now an **integration umbrella**, not a build story. **Ask: are we retiring/reframing SFCC-92 (and 293/295) so each thing is built exactly once — components in Epic 2, page assembly in Epic 5?** Confirm the mental model: *Epic 4 config → Epic 2 components → Epic 5 page integration.*

## Cross-cutting decisions to raise once

| # | Point | Ask |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **WCAG version.** All 3 draft component ACs say "WCAG **2.1** AA minimum." | Project standard is **2.2 AA** (AGENTS.md). Raise the bar in the AC template, or these bake in the wrong target. |
| 2 | **Colour model is now resolved — but dual.** SFCC-25 = natural variants as variation groups (in-master, no reload); SFCC-708 = cross-product colours via `Related Colours` attribute (new style code + full reload). | SFCC-91 must handle **both swatch types on one PDP** + the new gallery rollover-preview (Dani, today). This *dissolves* the "AC contradicts itself" I raised — but SFCC-91's AC must be split by scenario. |
| 3 | **Unestimated stories already in active Sprint 3.** SFCC-268 and SFCC-434 are in Sprint 3 (10–24 Aug) with **no points**. | Point them or pull them. Everything else here is also unpointed. |
| 4 | **None of the 10 are estimated.** | Suggested points below to anchor discussion. |

---

# Group A — Draft component stories (early feedback for Jasmijn)

These are genuinely well-written — the props-only boundaries and explicit a11y ACs are exactly right for our component conventions (container/presentational split, Storybook-per-component). Feedback is refinement, not rework.

## SFCC-648 `pdp/size-selector` (Epic 2 · High · To Do)

Strongest of the three — 21 ACs, thorough keyboard/SR coverage. Blocks SFCC-92 & SFCC-150.

| Angle | Feedback / question |
|---|---|
| Behaviour | Six size states (in-stock / low / OOS / notify-me / **recommended** / error). Clean. |
| ⚠️ Data | **"Recommended" state source?** That's Measmerize (PRD-050) — a 3rd-party overlay. How does the prop reach the selector? Integration path unclear. |
| Data | Stock status is props-in (good) — but confirm the **container** deriving in/low/OOS from buffer threshold is owned elsewhere (SFCC-239/293), not here. |
| Coupling | AC#9/#16 "error state triggered externally by Add-to-Bag" — define the **contract** between size-selector and add-to-bag (shared state via `pdp/hero`). |
| A11y | Excellent (arrow keys, Enter/Space, stock status in accessible name, live-region errors). Just bump 2.1 → 2.2. |
| Estimate | ~**5** (state matrix + full keyboard model). |

## SFCC-650 `pdp/add-to-bag` (Epic 2 · High · To Do)

Cart API **is** in scope here (unlike old SFCC-92 which routed to OOTB cart). Blocks SFCC-92 & SFCC-150; relates to SFCC-196 (max qty) & SFCC-648.

| Angle | Feedback / question |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ A11y/behaviour | AC#1 says CTA is **`disabled`**, but AC#2 says a click shows "Size required" and AC#10 says it's **announced as unavailable**. A native `disabled` button can't be focused or clicked → use **`aria-disabled`** (focusable, intercepts click, announced). Reconcile the three ACs to that pattern. |
| Behaviour | AC#5 "success state" is vague — is it a toast, the mini-bag opening, or the header count updating? Ties to SFCC-98 (fly-to-bag) + header bag count. Define it. |
| Behaviour | Error + retry path is good. Confirm optimistic vs pessimistic UI on the cart call. |
| Deps | Max-qty enforcement correctly out (SFCC-196) — but that means add-to-bag and max-qty both gate the same click; confirm order of checks. |
| Estimate | ~**5** (real cart mutation + loading/error/success states). |

## SFCC-723 `pdp/hero` (Epic 2 · High · To Do)

Pure layout/composition orchestrator — correct instinct (AC#8: owns no child logic).

| Angle | Feedback / question |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ Scope | The gallery it composes is a **custom carousel** (2×2 grid, video controls, dot indicator, "View Gallery" overlay). Base `image-gallery` does none of that. **Is the gallery/carousel a separate component story?** If it's bundled here, this isn't a hero story — it's 8+. |
| Dep | References **`pdp/product-content`** — not in this batch. Needs its own story before hero can integrate. |
| API | AC lists many composed children (carousel, product-content, colour picker, size selector, add-to-bag, drawer triggers). Define the **slot/prop contract** — named slots, not a loose `children`. |
| Dep | "View Gallery" opens the expanded gallery — that's where SFCC-708's rollover swatches live. Another component dependency. |
| A11y | Focus-order AC is good; 2.1 → 2.2. |
| Estimate | Hero-only ~**3**; **but split the gallery/carousel out first** or it balloons. |

---

# Group B — Approved, unestimated (re-read + what's changed)

## SFCC-25 Product Type & Variation Model (Epic 4 · Tech design)

Backend foundation for everything PDP. Confirms Master → Variation Group (colour) → Variant (colour+size SKU). Spike SFCC-120/247 done.

| Angle | Question |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ Data | **Open in comments (Dani → Jasmijn):** accessories with colour but **no size** — is the Variation Group purchasable, or do we force a "One Size" variant? Jasmijn proposes a 1-size variant SKU. Confirm and document — it affects `pdp/size-selector`'s one-size path. |
| Dependency | This gates SFCC-89/91/92/648/650 — it's the true "build first." Confirm sample product loaded in the test org. |
| Estimate | ~**3–5** (config + sample load). |

## SFCC-708 PDP – Related Colours Attribute — BM Config (Epic 4 · Ready for Review)

**This is the answer to last session's Model A/B question.** Comma-separated style codes link separate masters as cross-product colour swatches. Relates to SFCC-91.

| Angle | Question |
|---|---|
| Behaviour | Order of style codes = swatch display order; invalid ID → no save-time error, **skipped at render**. Testable, clean. |
| ⚠️ New (Dani, today 13 Aug) | Two behaviours just added that aren't in SFCC-91 yet: (1) related colour **not enabled due to stock → swatch hidden**; (2) in the **expanded gallery, swatch rollover previews images with no page load**. Flow these into SFCC-91 / the gallery story. |
| Data | FE fetches N related products per PDP → watch the request cost (batch/parallel, not waterfall; prefetch on hover). |
| Estimate | BM config ~**2–3**; the FE render/test lives in SFCC-91. |

## SFCC-196 PDP UI – Maximum Purchase Quantity (Epic 5 · Tech design)

Now cleanly scoped after the split. No qty selector on PDP → enforcement = counting repeat Add-to-Bags of the same variant.

| Angle | Question |
|---|---|
| Behaviour | Resolved: per-group/SKU override **split to enhancement SFCC-703**; global default (3) only here. Confirm final precedence rule for later (Emma: SKU < group < default, lowest-level wins). |
| Behaviour | Limit is per **size variant** already in bag — needs live basket read on the PDP. Confirm behaviour across colour variants (AC#3). |
| Deps | SFCC-268 (BM config) provides the value; SFCC-250 (cart enforcement) is the sibling. Enforced by `pdp/add-to-bag`. |
| Estimate | ~**3–5**. |

## SFCC-268 Max Purchase Quantity – BM Config (Epic 4 · Tech design · **in Sprint 3**)

Global default config; fallback when no SKU/group override (SFCC-703).

| Angle | Question |
|---|---|
| Behaviour | Blank = no restriction (AC#4). Value applied at **size-variant** level (AC#2). |
| Estimate | Small BM config ~**2**. In the sprint but unpointed. |

## SFCC-434 PDP – Add to Wishlist (Epic 5 · Tech design · **in Sprint 3** · High)

Leans on OOTB SFCC customer product-lists (Mani confirmed OOTB, incl. OOS-to-wishlist). This effectively **resolves the SFCC-vs-Omneo wishlist open item** in favour of SFCC-hosted for launch — worth confirming explicitly.

| Angle | Question |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ Behaviour | **CRM-127/128 (one size per *product*) vs AC#6 (one size per *colour variant*, each colour independent).** Unreconciled — Jasmijn flagged. Current site = one per product. Which wins? |
| Behaviour | Save size before wishlisting; guest → OOTB login (auth modal out of scope, in Wishlist epic). Icon reflects **per-colour-variant** state → custom logic over OOTB. |
| UX | Deselect removes from wishlist → so the icon must **reset on size change** (Jasmijn's open point). Confirm the interaction. |
| Scope | Confirmation message **split to SFCC-710**; OOS-to-wishlist tracked in SFCC-168. |
| A11y | Icon-only button needs `aria-label` + pressed/active state announced. |
| Estimate | ~**5** (custom icon-state logic on OOTB API). Unpointed but in the sprint. |

## SFCC-132 PDP UI – Product Badges (Epic 5 · Blocked · High)

Approved (Emma, 30 Jul). **This confirms badges are their own story — remove them from SFCC-89's scope** (the gap I flagged last time).

| Angle | Question |
|---|---|
| Deps | **Blocked by SFCC-225** (badge creation/assignment/priority BM config, Ready for Review). Priority hierarchy is defined there — confirm it's available. |
| ⚠️ Behaviour | Clickable badge → **filtered PLP** needs the PLP + a badge-filter mechanism to exist. PLP isn't built. Sequencing/placeholder? |
| Behaviour | Multi-badge priority order, **locale-specific labels**, **region-gated** badges (AU-only), VIC Exclusive = customer-group gated. Real complexity. |
| Data | Shares display logic with the PLP tile (SFCC-236 Product Card) — coordinate so badge rendering is one component, not two. |
| Estimate | ~**5** (priority + i18n + region/group gating + click-through). |

## SFCC-84 Recently Viewed – See Full History (Epic 7 · Tech design)

Follow-up page behind the rail's "See Full History" link (rail = SFCC-83).

| Angle | Question |
|---|---|
| ⚠️ Data | Same **storage-backend question as SFCC-83 still open** (guest session vs authenticated cross-device). The full-history page reads the same store — can't finalise until that's decided. |
| Behaviour | Note the tile treatment differs: **rail = image-only** (SFCC-83) vs **full page = full PLP-style card** (AC#2, per SFCC-80). Confirm that's intended. |
| Deps | **Blocked by SFCC-236** (Product Card shared component, Ready for Review) + SFCC-80 (PLP tile). |
| Scope | Emma's Contentful-refactor question **withdrawn** — images are SFCC, not Contentful. |
| Estimate | ~**3** (page reusing the shared card). |

---

## Suggested story points to seat the discussion

| Story | Suggested | Confidence / risk |
|---|---|---|
| SFCC-648 size-selector | 5 | Solid |
| SFCC-650 add-to-bag | 5 | Resolve disabled/aria-disabled + success UX first |
| SFCC-723 pdp/hero | 3 (hero only) | **Split gallery/carousel out** or it's 8+ |
| SFCC-25 variation model | 3–5 | Config; resolve accessories/one-size |
| SFCC-708 related colours | 2–3 | BM config; FE test in SFCC-91 |
| SFCC-196 max-qty UI | 3–5 | Needs live basket read |
| SFCC-268 max-qty config | 2 | Small |
| SFCC-434 wishlist | 5 | Reconcile CRM-127/128 vs per-colour |
| SFCC-132 badges | 5 | Blocked by 225 + PLP |
| SFCC-84 see full history | 3 | Blocked by 236/80; storage TBD |

## What I'd action out of the room
1. **Confirm the two-track model** and reframe/retire SFCC-92 (+ 293/295) so Epic-2 components aren't rebuilt as Epic-5 stories.
2. **Update SFCC-91** to cover *both* swatch types + the new SFCC-708 gallery-rollover + stock-gated visibility (Dani, today).
3. **Two product decisions:** wishlist one-size-per-product vs per-colour (SFCC-434); accessories no-size variant handling (SFCC-25).
4. **Fix the component-AC template:** WCAG 2.2, and the `aria-disabled` add-to-bag pattern.
5. **Point the two Sprint-3 stories** (268, 434) now.
