## 4. Full story detail

### SFCC-723 — `pdp/hero`

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-062, PRD-063, PRD-064, PRD-065, `pdp/hero`*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/hero` React component built to the Zimmermann Design System
> 2026 spec, so that it can be used as the top-level orchestration component for the PDP, composing
> the product image gallery and `pdp/product-content` into a single, responsive hero layout.
>
> The component is responsible for layout and composition only — it does not own the interaction
> logic of its child components. It accepts child components as composed instances (e.g. carousel,
> `pdp/product-content`, colour picker, size selector, add-to-bag, drawer triggers) and manages their
> arrangement across desktop and mobile breakpoints. The sole configuration prop is
> `showGalleryButton` (boolean), which controls whether the "View Gallery" CTA button overlay appears
> on the image gallery.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Layout — Desktop*
1. Desktop breakpoint: image gallery left, `pdp/product-content` right, spacing/proportions per design system.
2. Desktop gallery displays carousel items in sequence: single full-width images, and a 4-up 2x2 grid with a View Gallery button overlay on the bottom-right image.
3. Desktop carousel with a video item: video control icons (mute, play/pause) visible bottom-right of that item.

*Layout — Mobile*
4. Mobile breakpoint: gallery full-width top, `pdp/product-content` below in stacked column with padding per design system.
5. Mobile: dot-indicator carousel bar visible bottom-left, showing current position across available images.

*showGalleryButton prop*
6. `showGalleryButton` true → View Gallery button overlay visible.
7. `showGalleryButton` false → no View Gallery button overlay.

*Child component composition*
8. Does not replicate or override child interaction logic — size validation, add-to-bag API calls, drawer open/close, colour swatch selection are owned by their respective child stories.

*Responsiveness*
9. Viewport transitions between mobile and desktop switch layout between stacked and side-by-side with no layout breakage.

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
10. Keyboard focus order follows visual reading order: gallery first on desktop (left), product content second (right); stacked top-to-bottom on mobile.
11. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum; child component accessibility covered in their stories.

---

### SFCC-737 — `pdp/product-content`

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/product-content` React component built to the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/hero` to render the full product
> information panel on the PDP.
>
> The component is a composition container. It does not own the logic of its child components —
> interaction behaviour for colour selection, size selection, add to bag, wishlist, and drawer
> triggers are covered in their respective child component stories. This story covers the layout,
> ordering, and rendering of all child elements within the panel, and the static content elements
> (product name, description, model description, style code) that are not extracted into separate
> components.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Composition & layout*
1. Renders elements top to bottom per design system: product name + wishlist icon, price, product description, `pdp/product-colour-picker`, `pdp/size-selector`, `pdp/add-to-bag`, Find in Boutique link, drawer trigger rows (Details & Care, Size & Fit, Shipping & Returns, Assistance), model description, style code.
2. Desktop layout and spacing match design system spec.
3. Mobile layout and spacing match mobile design system spec.

*Static content*
4. Product name displays in uppercase using heading typography style.
5. Product description displays below the price in body typography style.
6. Model description displays below drawer triggers in caption typography style.
7. Style code displays at bottom of panel in subtle text colour.

*Find in Boutique link*
8. Find in Boutique link visible below Add to Bag CTA; fires the Find in Boutique panel trigger on click — panel itself out of scope.

*Empty & error states*
9. No product description → element does not render, no empty space left.
10. No model description → element does not render.
11. No style code → element does not render.

*Accessibility*
12. Keyboard focus order follows visual top-to-bottom reading order.
13. Product name marked up as a heading at the appropriate level in the page hierarchy.
14. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

---

### SFCC-731 — `pdp/carousel`

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-061, PRD-063, PRD-064, PRD-065, PRD-066*
*Blocks: SFCC-186 (PDP – Product Image Gallery)*

> ⚠️ **The Acceptance Criteria field is empty on this ticket.** The ACs below live in the
> description, and the numbering is mangled by Jira auto-numbering (all rendered as "1."). Some
> layout separators also appear to have been stripped (e.g. "2 full-width  2-up grid" likely means
> "2 full-width + 2-up grid").

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/carousel` React component built to the Zimmermann Design
> System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/hero` to render the product image and video
> gallery on the PDP.
>
> The component renders a sequence of media items (photo and video) in a stacked layout on desktop
> and a swipeable carousel on mobile. The desktop layout adapts based on total media count. Video is
> treated as a standard media item and slots into the layout based on its position in the product's
> media array. The component renders a View Gallery button as a trigger only — the gallery overlay is
> a separate component and out of scope for this story.

**Acceptance criteria (as written in the description)**

*Desktop layout — media count thresholds*
1. 3 media items → 3 full-width stacked + View Gallery button
2. 4 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery button
3. 5 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery 1 button
4. 6 media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery button
5. 7 media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery X button (X = total minus 6)
6. Video items slot into layout based on position in the media array — not treated differently to photos for layout purposes.

*showGalleryButton prop*
7. `showGalleryButton` false → no View Gallery button regardless of media count.
8. `showGalleryButton` true → View Gallery button renders per thresholds above, visible and tappable — overlay behaviour out of scope.

*Mobile*
9. Mobile: all media items display in a swipeable single-image carousel with dot indicator bar regardless of media count.
10. Swipe → active dot indicator updates to reflect current position.
11. `showGalleryButton` true on mobile → View Gallery button visible and tappable.

*Empty & error states*
12. No media items → component does not render, no broken layout.
13. Image fails to load → surrounding layout maintained without a broken image rendering — fallback behaviour TBD, see open items.

*Accessibility*
14. Carousel fully keyboard navigable and meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

**Open items (in ticket)**
- @Kiera — confirm media count threshold logic is correct per design specs shared.
- @Kiera — confirm fallback behaviour when an image fails to load (blank space, grey box, or branded fallback image).

---

### SFCC-739 — `pdp/gallery`  ❌ *design componentisation pending*

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-063, PRD-065*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/gallery` React component built to the Zimmermann Design
> System 2026 spec, so that it can be triggered from `pdp/carousel` to render a full-screen product
> image gallery overlay on the PDP.
>
> The component renders a full-screen overlay containing a sticky `pdp/gallery-header` and a
> scrollable vertical stack of `pdp/carousel/item` instances. It is triggered by the View Gallery
> button in `pdp/carousel` and manages its own open/close state. It does not own the carousel or
> product content — it receives the product media array as a prop and renders it within the gallery
> layout.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Overlay shell*
1. View Gallery button clicked in `pdp/carousel` → gallery opens full-screen, taking over entire viewport.
2. Gallery open → clicking close icon dismisses overlay and returns shopper to previous scroll position on the PDP.

*`pdp/gallery-header` — Desktop*
3. Desktop: gallery header sticky at top of overlay, remains visible while scrolling images.
4. Desktop header displays: product name, active colour name, close icon, model avatar thumbnails.
5. Product with multiple colour variants → header includes a colour selector in addition to the active colour name.
6. Clicking a model avatar thumbnail → gallery scrolls to the corresponding image set for that model.
7. Close icon clicked → gallery closes and focus returns to the View Gallery button that opened it.

*`pdp/gallery-header` — Mobile*
8. Mobile: gallery header sticky at top of overlay, remains visible while scrolling.
9. Mobile header displays: product name, close icon, colour selector. Model avatar thumbnails **not** shown on mobile.

*Image content*
10. Full media array renders as a vertically scrollable stack of `pdp/carousel/item` instances.
11. Images served in optimised format at appropriate resolution per breakpoint (PRD-063).

*Empty & error states*
12. No media items provided → gallery does not open, no broken layout.
13. Image fails to load within gallery → image slot maintains dimensions without breaking layout.

*Accessibility*
14. Gallery opens → focus moves into overlay and is trapped within it until closed.
15. Gallery closes → focus returns to the View Gallery button that triggered it.
16. Overlay has `role=dialog` and appropriate `aria-label`.
17. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

**Open items (in ticket)**
- @Kiera — gallery overlay and `pdp/gallery-header` not yet componentised in Design System Figma. Design exists in Designs file (`QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs`, node `3093-81721`). Extract into named components before dev picks this up.
- @Kiera — confirm AC6: does clicking a model avatar thumbnail scroll to a specific image, or filter the gallery to show only that model's images?

---

### SFCC-734 — `pdp/product-colour-picker`

*Labels: PRD-069*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/product-colour-picker` React component built to the
> Zimmermann Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/product-content` to render
> the colour swatch selector on the PDP.
>
> The component renders a row of colour swatches, a "Colour:" label, and the name of the currently
> selected colour. Each swatch displays a cropped product image thumbnail. The component manages
> selected and unselected swatch states. It does not own the cross-component interactions triggered
> by swatch selection or hover — those are covered in the relevant page-level stories.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Rendering*
1. "Colour:" label and active colour name display above the swatch row.
2. Each swatch displays a product image thumbnail at equal width.
3. Selected swatch renders with a visible bottom border indicator per design system.
4. Unselected swatch renders without the border indicator.

*Interaction*
5. Click a swatch → that swatch becomes selected and the colour name label updates.
6. Click an already-selected swatch → no state change.

*Empty & error states*
7. Only one colour variant → no swatch row renders; only "Colour:" label and colour name displayed.
8. Swatch image fails to load → swatch slot maintains dimensions without breaking layout.

*Accessibility*
9. Each swatch focusable and selectable via keyboard.
10. Each swatch has an `aria-label` describing the colour name (e.g. "Raspberry").
11. Selected swatch has `aria-pressed="true"`; unselected have `aria-pressed="false"`.
12. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

---

### SFCC-648 — `pdp/size-selector`

*Labels: PRD-012, PRD-014, PRD-016, `pdp/size-selector`*
*Blocks: SFCC-92, SFCC-150 · Relates: SFCC-650*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/size-selector` React component built to the Zimmermann
> design system spec, so that it can be consumed by PDP and any other page-level stories that require
> size selection.
>
> The component should be built as a standalone PWA Kit React component, sourced from the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 Figma file. It renders a size selector UI displaying available sizes with their
> stock status. It does not handle inventory API integration — stock status is passed in as props.
> For one-size products, the standard selector UI is suppressed and replaced with a plain "One size"
> label.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Rendered with a list of sizes, no size selected → selector displays default state with placeholder label.
2. Shopper selects a size → selector displays filled state showing the selected size.
3. Selector in focus/open → renders active state showing all size options.
4. Size with stock status *in stock* → displays as standard selectable option.
5. Size with stock status *low stock* → displays with low availability indicator per design spec (PRD-012).
6. Size with stock status *out of stock* → renders as non-selectable, visually disabled option (PRD-014).
7. Size with stock status *notify me* → renders with Notify Me label per design spec (PRD-016); the Notify Me interaction itself handled by a separate story.
8. Size with status *recommended* → displays with a recommended indicator per design spec.
9. No valid size selected and selector in error state (triggered externally, e.g. by Add to Bag) → error state renders per design.
10. Rendered on mobile → renders using the mobile variant per design system spec.
11. Product has only one size → standard size selector UI not displayed; plain "One size" text label rendered in its place per approved PDP designs (PDP Low availability frame, file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs`).
12. Product has only one size → size automatically considered selected; no shopper interaction required to enable Add to Bag.

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
13. Keyboard user tabs to selector → visible focus ring per design system spec.
14. Arrow Up / Arrow Down → focus moves between size options without a mouse.
15. Enter or Space on a focused size option → that size is selected.
16. Error state triggered → focus retained on or moved to the selector so the user is aware.
17. Screen reader on a size option with a stock status indicator → stock status included in the accessible label, e.g. "Size 1 (US 6), Low Availability".
18. Error state with message → announced via ARIA live region without navigation.
19. Out-of-stock, non-selectable size option → announced as unavailable rather than skipped or only visually greyed.
20. One-size product with "One size" label → announced correctly as the selected size.
21. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum.

---

### SFCC-650 — `pdp/add-to-bag`

*Labels: PRD-018*
*Blocks: SFCC-92, SFCC-150 · Relates: SFCC-648, SFCC-196*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/add-to-bag` React component built for the Zimmermann PWA
> Kit, so that it can be consumed by the PDP and any other page-level stories that require
> add-to-bag functionality.
>
> The component renders using the base Button component (Primary, Large) from the Zimmermann design
> system. It wraps it with add-to-bag-specific interaction logic: size selection validation, stock
> state awareness, loading state during cart API call, and inline error messaging. **Cart API
> integration is in scope for this story.** Maximum purchase quantity enforcement is handled
> separately in SFCC-196.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. No size selected on page load → Add to Bag CTA displayed but **disabled**.
2. Click Add to Bag without selecting a size → button remains inactive and "Size required" inline message displayed.
3. Select an in-stock size → Add to Bag CTA becomes active and enabled.
4. Click Add to Bag with valid size → cart API call made, button displays loading state while in flight.
5. Cart API call succeeds → item confirmed as added to bag and appropriate success state shown.
6. Cart API call fails → inline error message displayed, CTA returns to enabled state so shopper can retry.
7. One-size product → size treated as pre-selected, Add to Bag CTA active on page load.
8. Component accepts size selection state and stock status as props — does not manage size selection itself; that is owned by `pdp/size-selector` (SFCC-648).

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
9. Keyboard user tabs to CTA → visible focus ring per design system spec.
10. CTA in disabled state → announced as unavailable to screen reader users.
11. Inline error or success message → announced via ARIA live region without navigation.
12. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum.

---

### SFCC-735 — `pdp/drawer-trigger`

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/drawer-trigger` React component built to the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be used within `pdp/product-content` to render each
> accordion trigger row on the PDP (Details & Care, Size & Fit, Shipping & Returns, Assistance).
>
> The component renders a label and an expand/collapse icon. It manages its own open and closed
> visual state. It does not own the drawer/modal content that appears on activation — it is
> responsible for rendering the trigger and firing the open event only.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Rendering*
1. Label and expand icon display in a single row per design system.
2. Closed state → expand icon renders in default orientation.
3. Open state → expand icon renders in active orientation.

*Interaction*
4. Click trigger → toggles between open and closed state, fires drawer open event.
5. Open and clicked again → returns to closed state, fires drawer close event.

*Empty & error states*
6. No label provided → component does not render.

*Accessibility*
7. Keyboard focusable and activatable.
8. Appropriate `aria-expanded` reflecting open (true) / closed (false).
9. `aria-controls` referencing the drawer panel it controls.
10. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

---

### SFCC-736 — `pdp/drawer`

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/drawer` React component built to the Zimmermann Design
> System 2026 spec, so that it can be used on the PDP to render the slide-in panel that houses tabbed
> product information (Details & Care, Size Guide, Find My Size, Shipping & Returns, Assistance).
>
> The component is responsible for the drawer shell only — the slide-in panel, overlay backdrop,
> close button, and tab navigation header. It does not own the content rendered within each tab; that
> is covered in the relevant PDP functional stories (**SFCC-102, SFCC-101, SFCC-195, SFCC-266,
> SFCC-267**). The component accepts tab content as children.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Rendering*
1. Drawer triggered → slides in from the right per design system.
2. Drawer open → backdrop overlay renders behind panel covering rest of page.
3. Drawer open → close icon visible top-right of panel, closes drawer on click.
4. Drawer open → tab navigation header renders with correct tab labels as passed via props.
5. Active tab renders in selected state per design system.
6. Inactive tab renders in default state.
7. Click a tab → that tab becomes active and corresponding content area updates.

*Behaviour*
8. Drawer open → clicking backdrop overlay closes the drawer.
9. Drawer open on mobile → panel renders full-width from bottom or right per design system.
10. Content exceeds panel height → content area scrolls independently without tab header scrolling.

*Empty & error states*
11. No tab content provided → drawer shell still renders without breaking layout.

*Accessibility*
12. Drawer opens → focus moves to drawer panel and is trapped until closed.
13. Drawer closes → focus returns to the trigger element that opened it.
14. Tabs navigable via keyboard.
15. `role=dialog` and appropriate `aria-label`.
16. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

---

### SFCC-740 — `pdp/find-in-boutique`  ❌ *design componentisation pending*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/find-in-boutique` React component built to the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 spec, so that it renders as a slide-in panel from the right on the PDP when the
> Find in Boutique link is clicked.

## 4. Full story detail

### SFCC-723 — `pdp/hero`

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-062, PRD-063, PRD-064, PRD-065, `pdp/hero`*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/hero` React component built to the Zimmermann Design System
> 2026 spec, so that it can be used as the top-level orchestration component for the PDP, composing
> the product image gallery and `pdp/product-content` into a single, responsive hero layout.
>
> The component is responsible for layout and composition only — it does not own the interaction
> logic of its child components. It accepts child components as composed instances (e.g. carousel,
> `pdp/product-content`, colour picker, size selector, add-to-bag, drawer triggers) and manages their
> arrangement across desktop and mobile breakpoints. The sole configuration prop is
> `showGalleryButton` (boolean), which controls whether the "View Gallery" CTA button overlay appears
> on the image gallery.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Layout — Desktop*
1. Desktop breakpoint: image gallery left, `pdp/product-content` right, spacing/proportions per design system.
2. Desktop gallery displays carousel items in sequence: single full-width images, and a 4-up 2x2 grid with a View Gallery button overlay on the bottom-right image.
3. Desktop carousel with a video item: video control icons (mute, play/pause) visible bottom-right of that item.

*Layout — Mobile*
4. Mobile breakpoint: gallery full-width top, `pdp/product-content` below in stacked column with padding per design system.
5. Mobile: dot-indicator carousel bar visible bottom-left, showing current position across available images.

*showGalleryButton prop*
6. `showGalleryButton` true → View Gallery button overlay visible.
7. `showGalleryButton` false → no View Gallery button overlay.

*Child component composition*
8. Does not replicate or override child interaction logic — size validation, add-to-bag API calls, drawer open/close, colour swatch selection are owned by their respective child stories.

*Responsiveness*
9. Viewport transitions between mobile and desktop switch layout between stacked and side-by-side with no layout breakage.

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
10. Keyboard focus order follows visual reading order: gallery first on desktop (left), product content second (right); stacked top-to-bottom on mobile.
11. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum; child component accessibility covered in their stories.

---

### SFCC-737 — `pdp/product-content`

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/product-content` React component built to the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/hero` to render the full product
> information panel on the PDP.
>
> The component is a composition container. It does not own the logic of its child components —
> interaction behaviour for colour selection, size selection, add to bag, wishlist, and drawer
> triggers are covered in their respective child component stories. This story covers the layout,
> ordering, and rendering of all child elements within the panel, and the static content elements
> (product name, description, model description, style code) that are not extracted into separate
> components.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Composition & layout*
1. Renders elements top to bottom per design system: product name + wishlist icon, price, product description, `pdp/product-colour-picker`, `pdp/size-selector`, `pdp/add-to-bag`, Find in Boutique link, drawer trigger rows (Details & Care, Size & Fit, Shipping & Returns, Assistance), model description, style code.
2. Desktop layout and spacing match design system spec.
3. Mobile layout and spacing match mobile design system spec.

*Static content*
4. Product name displays in uppercase using heading typography style.
5. Product description displays below the price in body typography style.
6. Model description displays below drawer triggers in caption typography style.
7. Style code displays at bottom of panel in subtle text colour.

*Find in Boutique link*
8. Find in Boutique link visible below Add to Bag CTA; fires the Find in Boutique panel trigger on click — panel itself out of scope.

*Empty & error states*
9. No product description → element does not render, no empty space left.
10. No model description → element does not render.
11. No style code → element does not render.

*Accessibility*
12. Keyboard focus order follows visual top-to-bottom reading order.
13. Product name marked up as a heading at the appropriate level in the page hierarchy.
14. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

### SFCC-731 — `pdp/carousel`

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-061, PRD-063, PRD-064, PRD-065, PRD-066*
*Blocks: SFCC-186 (PDP – Product Image Gallery)*

> ⚠️ **The Acceptance Criteria field is empty on this ticket.** The ACs below live in the
> description, and the numbering is mangled by Jira auto-numbering (all rendered as "1."). Some
> layout separators also appear to have been stripped (e.g. "2 full-width  2-up grid" likely means
> "2 full-width + 2-up grid").

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/carousel` React component built to the Zimmermann Design
> System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/hero` to render the product image and video
> gallery on the PDP.
>
> The component renders a sequence of media items (photo and video) in a stacked layout on desktop
> and a swipeable carousel on mobile. The desktop layout adapts based on total media count. Video is
> treated as a standard media item and slots into the layout based on its position in the product's
> media array. The component renders a View Gallery button as a trigger only — the gallery overlay is
> a separate component and out of scope for this story.

**Acceptance criteria (as written in the description)**

*Desktop layout — media count thresholds*
1. 3 media items → 3 full-width stacked + View Gallery button
2. 4 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery button
3. 5 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery 1 button
4. 6 media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery button
5. 7 media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery X button (X = total minus 6)
6. Video items slot into layout based on position in the media array — not treated differently to photos for layout purposes.

*showGalleryButton prop*
7. `showGalleryButton` false → no View Gallery button regardless of media count.
8. `showGalleryButton` true → View Gallery button renders per thresholds above, visible and tappable — overlay behaviour out of scope.

*Mobile*
9. Mobile: all media items display in a swipeable single-image carousel with dot indicator bar regardless of media count.
10. Swipe → active dot indicator updates to reflect current position.
11. `showGalleryButton` true on mobile → View Gallery button visible and tappable.

*Empty & error states*
12. No media items → component does not render, no broken layout.
13. Image fails to load → surrounding layout maintained without a broken image rendering — fallback behaviour TBD, see open items.

*Accessibility*
14. Carousel fully keyboard navigable and meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

**Open items (in ticket)**
- @Kiera — confirm media count threshold logic is correct per design specs shared.
- @Kiera — confirm fallback behaviour when an image fails to load (blank space, grey box, or branded fallback image).

### SFCC-739 — `pdp/gallery`  ❌ *design componentisation pending*

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-063, PRD-065*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/gallery` React component built to the Zimmermann Design
> System 2026 spec, so that it can be triggered from `pdp/carousel` to render a full-screen product
> image gallery overlay on the PDP.
>
> The component renders a full-screen overlay containing a sticky `pdp/gallery-header` and a
> scrollable vertical stack of `pdp/carousel/item` instances. It is triggered by the View Gallery
> button in `pdp/carousel` and manages its own open/close state. It does not own the carousel or
> product content — it receives the product media array as a prop and renders it within the gallery
> layout.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Overlay shell*
1. View Gallery button clicked in `pdp/carousel` → gallery opens full-screen, taking over entire viewport.
2. Gallery open → clicking close icon dismisses overlay and returns shopper to previous scroll position on the PDP.

*`pdp/gallery-header` — Desktop*
3. Desktop: gallery header sticky at top of overlay, remains visible while scrolling images.
4. Desktop header displays: product name, active colour name, close icon, model avatar thumbnails.
5. Product with multiple colour variants → header includes a colour selector in addition to the active colour name.
6. Clicking a model avatar thumbnail → gallery scrolls to the corresponding image set for that model.
7. Close icon clicked → gallery closes and focus returns to the View Gallery button that opened it.

*`pdp/gallery-header` — Mobile*
8. Mobile: gallery header sticky at top of overlay, remains visible while scrolling.
9. Mobile header displays: product name, close icon, colour selector. Model avatar thumbnails **not** shown on mobile.

*Image content*
10. Full media array renders as a vertically scrollable stack of `pdp/carousel/item` instances.
11. Images served in optimised format at appropriate resolution per breakpoint (PRD-063).

*Empty & error states*
12. No media items provided → gallery does not open, no broken layout.
13. Image fails to load within gallery → image slot maintains dimensions without breaking layout.

*Accessibility*
14. Gallery opens → focus moves into overlay and is trapped within it until closed.
15. Gallery closes → focus returns to the View Gallery button that triggered it.
16. Overlay has `role=dialog` and appropriate `aria-label`.
17. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

**Open items (in ticket)**

### SFCC-734 — `pdp/product-colour-picker`

*Labels: PRD-069*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/product-colour-picker` React component built to the
> Zimmermann Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/product-content` to render
> the colour swatch selector on the PDP.
>
> The component renders a row of colour swatches, a "Colour:" label, and the name of the currently
> selected colour. Each swatch displays a cropped product image thumbnail. The component manages
> selected and unselected swatch states. It does not own the cross-component interactions triggered
> by swatch selection or hover — those are covered in the relevant page-level stories.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Rendering*
1. "Colour:" label and active colour name display above the swatch row.
2. Each swatch displays a product image thumbnail at equal width.
3. Selected swatch renders with a visible bottom border indicator per design system.
4. Unselected swatch renders without the border indicator.

*Interaction*
5. Click a swatch → that swatch becomes selected and the colour name label updates.
6. Click an already-selected swatch → no state change.

*Empty & error states*
7. Only one colour variant → no swatch row renders; only "Colour:" label and colour name displayed.
8. Swatch image fails to load → swatch slot maintains dimensions without breaking layout.

*Accessibility*
9. Each swatch focusable and selectable via keyboard.
10. Each swatch has an `aria-label` describing the colour name (e.g. "Raspberry").
11. Selected swatch has `aria-pressed="true"`; unselected have `aria-pressed="false"`.
12. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

### SFCC-648 — `pdp/size-selector`

*Labels: PRD-012, PRD-014, PRD-016, `pdp/size-selector`*
*Blocks: SFCC-92, SFCC-150 · Relates: SFCC-650*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/size-selector` React component built to the Zimmermann
> design system spec, so that it can be consumed by PDP and any other page-level stories that require
> size selection.
>
> The component should be built as a standalone PWA Kit React component, sourced from the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 Figma file. It renders a size selector UI displaying available sizes with their
> stock status. It does not handle inventory API integration — stock status is passed in as props.
> For one-size products, the standard selector UI is suppressed and replaced with a plain "One size"
> label.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Rendered with a list of sizes, no size selected → selector displays default state with placeholder label.
2. Shopper selects a size → selector displays filled state showing the selected size.
3. Selector in focus/open → renders active state showing all size options.
4. Size with stock status *in stock* → displays as standard selectable option.
5. Size with stock status *low stock* → displays with low availability indicator per design spec (PRD-012).
6. Size with stock status *out of stock* → renders as non-selectable, visually disabled option (PRD-014).
7. Size with stock status *notify me* → renders with Notify Me label per design spec (PRD-016); the Notify Me interaction itself handled by a separate story.
8. Size with status *recommended* → displays with a recommended indicator per design spec.
9. No valid size selected and selector in error state (triggered externally, e.g. by Add to Bag) → error state renders per design.
10. Rendered on mobile → renders using the mobile variant per design system spec.
11. Product has only one size → standard size selector UI not displayed; plain "One size" text label rendered in its place per approved PDP designs (PDP Low availability frame, file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs`).
12. Product has only one size → size automatically considered selected; no shopper interaction required to enable Add to Bag.

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
13. Keyboard user tabs to selector → visible focus ring per design system spec.
14. Arrow Up / Arrow Down → focus moves between size options without a mouse.
15. Enter or Space on a focused size option → that size is selected.
16. Error state triggered → focus retained on or moved to the selector so the user is aware.
17. Screen reader on a size option with a stock status indicator → stock status included in the accessible label, e.g. "Size 1 (US 6), Low Availability".
18. Error state with message → announced via ARIA live region without navigation.
19. Out-of-stock, non-selectable size option → announced as unavailable rather than skipped or only visually greyed.
20. One-size product with "One size" label → announced correctly as the selected size.
21. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum.

---

### SFCC-650 — `pdp/add-to-bag`

*Labels: PRD-018*
*Blocks: SFCC-92, SFCC-150 · Relates: SFCC-648, SFCC-196*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/add-to-bag` React component built for the Zimmermann PWA
> Kit, so that it can be consumed by the PDP and any other page-level stories that require
> add-to-bag functionality.
>
> The component renders using the base Button component (Primary, Large) from the Zimmermann design
> system. It wraps it with add-to-bag-specific interaction logic: size selection validation, stock
> state awareness, loading state during cart API call, and inline error messaging. **Cart API
> integration is in scope for this story.** Maximum purchase quantity enforcement is handled
> separately in SFCC-196.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. No size selected on page load → Add to Bag CTA displayed but **disabled**.
2. Click Add to Bag without selecting a size → button remains inactive and "Size required" inline message displayed.
3. Select an in-stock size → Add to Bag CTA becomes active and enabled.
4. Click Add to Bag with valid size → cart API call made, button displays loading state while in flight.
5. Cart API call succeeds → item confirmed as added to bag and appropriate success state shown.
6. Cart API call fails → inline error message displayed, CTA returns to enabled state so shopper can retry.
7. One-size product → size treated as pre-selected, Add to Bag CTA active on page load.
8. Component accepts size selection state and stock status as props — does not manage size selection itself; that is owned by `pdp/size-selector` (SFCC-648).

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
9. Keyboard user tabs to CTA → visible focus ring per design system spec.
10. CTA in disabled state → announced as unavailable to screen reader users.
11. Inline error or success message → announced via ARIA live region without navigation.
12. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum.

### SFCC-735 — `pdp/drawer-trigger`

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/drawer-trigger` React component built to the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be used within `pdp/product-content` to render each
> accordion trigger row on the PDP (Details & Care, Size & Fit, Shipping & Returns, Assistance).
>
> The component renders a label and an expand/collapse icon. It manages its own open and closed
> visual state. It does not own the drawer/modal content that appears on activation — it is
> responsible for rendering the trigger and firing the open event only.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Rendering*
1. Label and expand icon display in a single row per design system.
2. Closed state → expand icon renders in default orientation.
3. Open state → expand icon renders in active orientation.

*Interaction*
4. Click trigger → toggles between open and closed state, fires drawer open event.
5. Open and clicked again → returns to closed state, fires drawer close event.

*Empty & error states*
6. No label provided → component does not render.

*Accessibility*
7. Keyboard focusable and activatable.
8. Appropriate `aria-expanded` reflecting open (true) / closed (false).
9. `aria-controls` referencing the drawer panel it controls.
10. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

### SFCC-736 — `pdp/drawer`

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/drawer` React component built to the Zimmermann Design
> System 2026 spec, so that it can be used on the PDP to render the slide-in panel that houses tabbed
> product information (Details & Care, Size Guide, Find My Size, Shipping & Returns, Assistance).
>
> The component is responsible for the drawer shell only — the slide-in panel, overlay backdrop,
> close button, and tab navigation header. It does not own the content rendered within each tab; that
> is covered in the relevant PDP functional stories (**SFCC-102, SFCC-101, SFCC-195, SFCC-266,
> SFCC-267**). The component accepts tab content as children.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Rendering*
1. Drawer triggered → slides in from the right per design system.
2. Drawer open → backdrop overlay renders behind panel covering rest of page.
3. Drawer open → close icon visible top-right of panel, closes drawer on click.
4. Drawer open → tab navigation header renders with correct tab labels as passed via props.
5. Active tab renders in selected state per design system.
6. Inactive tab renders in default state.
7. Click a tab → that tab becomes active and corresponding content area updates.

*Behaviour*
8. Drawer open → clicking backdrop overlay closes the drawer.
9. Drawer open on mobile → panel renders full-width from bottom or right per design system.
10. Content exceeds panel height → content area scrolls independently without tab header scrolling.

*Empty & error states*
11. No tab content provided → drawer shell still renders without breaking layout.

*Accessibility*
12. Drawer opens → focus moves to drawer panel and is trapped until closed.
13. Drawer closes → focus returns to the trigger element that opened it.
14. Tabs navigable via keyboard.
15. `role=dialog` and appropriate `aria-label`.
16. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

*Panel shell*

*Relates: SFCC-744 `product-card-group — Contentful`*

*Layout*

content.text:
Pulled all 13 and written to [pdpComponentStories.md](.docs/temp/pdpComponentStories.md) — summary table, composition tree, cross-references, and every description + AC transcribed verbatim so you can work from it without re-opening Jira.

**Snapshot:** all 13 are `To Do` · `High` · **unpointed** · no sprint · epic SFCC-2 · assigned to Jasmijn. Nine updated today.

---

## Four things I'd fix before it goes to business today

**1. SFCC-731 `pdp/carousel` has an empty Acceptance Criteria field.** The ACs are sitting in the description, and Jira's auto-numbering has mangled them into a list of "1."s with some separators stripped (`2 full-width  2-up grid` — presumably `+`). If it goes to sign-off like this, the business is approving a ticket whose AC field is blank. Two-minute fix.

**2. All 13 specify WCAG 2.1 AA.** Project standard is **2.2 AA** (AGENTS.md). This is the highest-leverage fix in the batch — once 13 tickets are business-signed-off at 2.1, changing it later means re-opening all of them.

**3. The drawer tab list contradicts itself across three places:**

| Source | List |
|---|---|
| SFCC-737 + SFCC-735 (triggers) | Details & Care · Size & Fit · Shipping & Returns · Assistance — **4** |
| SFCC-736 (drawer tabs) | Details & Care · **Size Guide** · **Find My Size** · Shipping & Returns · Assistance — **5** |
| `pdp.md` PRD-008 (confirmed) | Details · Size & Fit · Care · Shipping & Free Returns — **4, different names** |

The trigger rows and the drawer tabs don't match, and neither matches the confirmed PRD. These two tickets are going to sign-off together.

**4. SFCC-742 `wishlist/login-panel` bakes in an auth model.** AC#4–6 specify magic-link/OTP, Sign in with Apple, Sign in with Google. `projectState.md` records social login (ENH-004) as **SFCC OOTB config only, with a hard dependency on Apple/Google merchant accounts being provisioned — "do not implement until merchant accounts exist."** Business sign-off is arguably the right forum for this, but the ticket should say the dependency exists rather than implying it's settled.

---

## On the split itself — my read

**Broadly right.** The container/presentational boundaries are clean, "does not own X" appears in nearly every description, and the empty/error-state ACs are consistently present. That's better discipline than most component sets.

Three observations worth raising:

**Possibly too granular:** `pdp/drawer-trigger` (735) is a label + icon + `aria-expanded`. Per our own conventions, internal sub-components that only render inside one parent don't need their own story — cover them via the parent. It renders only inside `product-content`. Defensible either way (it's used 4× and has a real a11y contract), but worth a deliberate call rather than defaulting to a story.

**Possibly too split at the top:** `pdp/hero` (723) and `pdp/product-content` (737) are *both* pure composition containers that own no logic. Two orchestration stories whose combined job is "arrange children." Could reasonably be one.

**Genuinely missing — four components referenced but with no ticket:**

| Referenced as | Where | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `pdp/gallery-header` | SFCC-739 AC#3–9 | no story |
| `pdp/carousel/item` | SFCC-739 AC#10, description | no story |
| horizontal product card | SFCC-740 + SFCC-741 open items | no story — Jasmijn has flagged it herself |
| `ProductCard` atom | SFCC-743 AC#6 | is this SFCC-236? Not linked |

The horizontal product card is the sharp one: two panels depend on it, Jasmijn's own open item asks whether it's shared and what to call it, and there's already a vertical card component. That's a naming/ownership decision that should land before either panel is built.

**Also: 7 of 13 have no Jira links at all** (723, 737, 739, 734, 735, 736, 740, 742) despite the composition tree being explicit in the descriptions. The build order is invisible on the board.

---

Want me to do the full per-story pass next — same depth as the earlier reviews, with a suggested reply you can send Jasmijn? Given the EOD deadline I'd suggest I draft the reply first and go deep after, but happy either way.

I'm finding SFCC-186, the functional story for the Product Image Gallery, which is blocked by SFCC-731's carousel work. It describes a stacked editorial layout on desktop with a hero image, a second large image, and a 2x2 grid of supporting images, while mobile uses a full-width swipeable layout instead.

Two things stand out: the colour-switching behavior matches PRD-062's no-reload requirement, but there's a scope mismatch — SFCC-186 explicitly excludes video (pointing to SFCC-188), yet SFCC-731 and SFCC-723 both build in video handling for carousel items and hero control icons.

I also notice SFCC-195 claims ownership of "the slide out component and the first Details & Care tab," which directly overlaps with SFCC-736's claim to own the drawer shell — a duplicate claim worth flagging. And now there's a fourth, slightly different version of the drawer's tab list appearing in SFCC-195.

Comparing all four sources — SFCC-737/735, SFCC-736, SFCC-195, and pdp.md PRD-008 — each lists a different set of tabs with different names and counts, and the EU Environmental Qualities tab is conditional per locale, meaning the drawer's tab set isn't even fixed across all cases.

Looking at SFCC-102, it clarifies that Size & Fit/Size Guide acts as a fallback slide-out when Measmerize isn't configured for a product, while SFCC-101 establishes that the PDP always shows a Find My Size CTA, which opens the Measmerize flow when configured.

Once Measmerize generates a recommendation, selecting Continue auto-selects that size on the PDP — this directly explains where the "recommended" status in SFCC-648 AC#8 originates, so I should flag this as a useful cross-reference rather than a gap.

Checking SFCC-149 next: it's properly scoped to flow/submission while SFCC-741 covers the component build and accessibility, and the blocking relationship between them is consistent. Then SFCC-150 describes consistent UI behavior across the Coming Soon, Back in Soon, and Unavailable states — the size selector shows "Select size to get notified" with per-row Notify Me CTAs in the dropdown.

I'm noting two gaps: the placeholder text variant isn't mentioned in SFCC-648's AC#1, which only covers the default placeholder state, so this contextual variant seems undocumented. Also, Add to Bag being suppressed and replaced by a state label isn't covered by SFCC-650's ACs, which only address the disabled/enabled states for the no-size-selected path.

This also resolves something I'd flagged earlier — SFCC-150 explicitly confirms the size selector is a dropdown with a Notify Me CTA per size row, settling the swatch-vs-dropdown question from SFCC-648. I'm capturing that as a factual observation rather than a verdict.

This confirms the guest-prompt behavior in SFCC-742's login panel, and it reinforces the earlier contradiction I flagged — the PRD says one size per product, conflicting with SFCC-434's AC#6 which specifies one size per colour variant. ## 4. Full story detail + observations

### SFCC-723 — `pdp/hero`

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-062, PRD-063, PRD-064, PRD-065, `pdp/hero`*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/hero` React component built to the Zimmermann Design System
> 2026 spec, so that it can be used as the top-level orchestration component for the PDP, composing
> the product image gallery and `pdp/product-content` into a single, responsive hero layout.
>
> The component is responsible for layout and composition only — it does not own the interaction
> logic of its child components. It accepts child components as composed instances (e.g. carousel,
> `pdp/product-content`, colour picker, size selector, add-to-bag, drawer triggers) and manages their
> arrangement across desktop and mobile breakpoints. The sole configuration prop is
> `showGalleryButton` (boolean), which controls whether the "View Gallery" CTA button overlay appears
> on the image gallery.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Layout — Desktop*
1. Desktop breakpoint: image gallery left, `pdp/product-content` right, spacing/proportions per design system.
2. Desktop gallery displays carousel items in sequence: single full-width images, and a 4-up 2x2 grid with a View Gallery button overlay on the bottom-right image.
3. Desktop carousel with a video item: video control icons (mute, play/pause) visible bottom-right of that item.

*Layout — Mobile*
4. Mobile breakpoint: gallery full-width top, `pdp/product-content` below in stacked column with padding per design system.
5. Mobile: dot-indicator carousel bar visible bottom-left, showing current position across available images.

*showGalleryButton prop*
6. `showGalleryButton` true → View Gallery button overlay visible.
7. `showGalleryButton` false → no View Gallery button overlay.

*Child component composition*
8. Does not replicate or override child interaction logic — size validation, add-to-bag API calls, drawer open/close, colour swatch selection are owned by their respective child stories.

*Responsiveness*
9. Viewport transitions between mobile and desktop switch layout between stacked and side-by-side with no layout breakage.

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
10. Keyboard focus order follows visual reading order: gallery first on desktop (left), product content second (right); stacked top-to-bottom on mobile.
11. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum; child component accessibility covered in their stories.

**Observations**
- AC#2 (desktop gallery layout), AC#5 (mobile dot indicator) and AC#6–7 (`showGalleryButton`) specify behaviour that is **also specified in SFCC-731** (`pdp/carousel` AC#1–5, 7–8, 9–11). The same behaviour is described in two tickets.
- AC#3 covers video control icons. **SFCC-186 states video content in the gallery is out of scope (SFCC-188).**
- The description states the component owns "layout and composition only", while AC#2, #3 and #5 describe carousel internals.
- No Jira links; all children referenced in prose only.
- Accessibility target stated as WCAG 2.1 AA.

---

### SFCC-737 — `pdp/product-content`

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/product-content` React component built to the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/hero` to render the full product
> information panel on the PDP.
>
> The component is a composition container. It does not own the logic of its child components —
> interaction behaviour for colour selection, size selection, add to bag, wishlist, and drawer
> triggers are covered in their respective child component stories. This story covers the layout,
> ordering, and rendering of all child elements within the panel, and the static content elements
> (product name, description, model description, style code) that are not extracted into separate
> components.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Composition & layout*
1. Renders elements top to bottom per design system: product name + wishlist icon, price, product description, `pdp/product-colour-picker`, `pdp/size-selector`, `pdp/add-to-bag`, Find in Boutique link, drawer trigger rows (Details & Care, Size & Fit, Shipping & Returns, Assistance), model description, style code.
2. Desktop layout and spacing match design system spec.
3. Mobile layout and spacing match mobile design system spec.

*Static content*
4. Product name displays in uppercase using heading typography style.
5. Product description displays below the price in body typography style.
6. Model description displays below drawer triggers in caption typography style.
7. Style code displays at bottom of panel in subtle text colour.

*Find in Boutique link*
8. Find in Boutique link visible below Add to Bag CTA; fires the Find in Boutique panel trigger on click — panel itself out of scope.

*Empty & error states*
9. No product description → element does not render, no empty space left.
10. No model description → element does not render.
11. No style code → element does not render.

*Accessibility*
12. Keyboard focus order follows visual top-to-bottom reading order.
13. Product name marked up as a heading at the appropriate level in the page hierarchy.
14. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

**Observations**
- AC#1 lists **four** drawer triggers (Details & Care, Size & Fit, Shipping & Returns, Assistance). See §5 for the four differing tab/trigger lists across tickets and the PRD.
- AC#1 places a wishlist icon beside the product name. Wishlist behaviour is **SFCC-434**; the logged-out panel is **SFCC-742**. Neither is linked.
- AC#1 includes `price` as a single element. No AC covers Was/Now sale pricing (pdp.md §5, PRD-003).
- **No badge element appears in the layout order.** Badges are SFCC-132 (Blocked); not linked.
- AC#8 fires the Find in Boutique trigger; the panel is SFCC-740. Not linked.
- Empty-state ACs (#9–11) cover description, model description and style code. No empty/absent state is specified for price or for the colour picker.
- Accessibility target stated as WCAG 2.1 AA.

---

### SFCC-731 — `pdp/carousel`

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-061, PRD-063, PRD-064, PRD-065, PRD-066*
*Blocks: SFCC-186 (PDP – Product Image Gallery)*

> ⚠️ **The Acceptance Criteria field is empty on this ticket.** The ACs below live in the
> description, and the numbering is mangled by Jira auto-numbering (all rendered as "1."). Some
> layout separators also appear to have been stripped (e.g. "2 full-width  2-up grid" likely means
> "2 full-width + 2-up grid").

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/carousel` React component built to the Zimmermann Design
> System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/hero` to render the product image and video
> gallery on the PDP.
>
> The component renders a sequence of media items (photo and video) in a stacked layout on desktop
> and a swipeable carousel on mobile. The desktop layout adapts based on total media count. Video is
> treated as a standard media item and slots into the layout based on its position in the product's
> media array. The component renders a View Gallery button as a trigger only — the gallery overlay is
> a separate component and out of scope for this story.

**Acceptance criteria (as written in the description)**

*Desktop layout — media count thresholds*
1. 3 media items → 3 full-width stacked + View Gallery button
2. 4 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery button
3. 5 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery **1** button
4. 6 media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery button
5. 7 media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery **X** button (X = total minus 6)
6. Video items slot into layout based on position in the media array — not treated differently to photos for layout purposes.

*showGalleryButton prop*
7. `showGalleryButton` false → no View Gallery button regardless of media count.
8. `showGalleryButton` true → View Gallery button renders per thresholds above, visible and tappable — overlay behaviour out of scope.

*Mobile*
9. Mobile: all media items display in a swipeable single-image carousel with dot indicator bar regardless of media count.
10. Swipe → active dot indicator updates to reflect current position.
11. `showGalleryButton` true on mobile → View Gallery button visible and tappable.

*Empty & error states*
12. No media items → component does not render, no broken layout.
13. Image fails to load → surrounding layout maintained without a broken image rendering — fallback behaviour TBD, see open items.

*Accessibility*
14. Carousel fully keyboard navigable and meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

**Open items (in ticket)**
- @Kiera — confirm media count threshold logic is correct per design specs shared.
- @Kiera — confirm fallback behaviour when an image fails to load (blank space, grey box, or branded fallback image).

**Observations**
- **The Acceptance Criteria custom field is empty**; all ACs sit in the description body.
- Threshold rows 3 and 5 carry a numeric suffix on the button ("View Gallery 1", "View Gallery X"); rows 1, 2 and 4 do not. No threshold is given for 1, 2, or 8+ media items.
- AC#6 places video items in scope. **SFCC-186, which this story blocks, states video content in the gallery is out of scope (SFCC-188).**
- SFCC-186 describes the desktop layout as "large hero followed by another large image, then supporting images in a 2x2 grid" and contains no media-count thresholds.
- Layout and `showGalleryButton` behaviour is also specified in SFCC-723 AC#2, #5, #6–7.
- Accessibility target stated as WCAG 2.1 AA.

---

### SFCC-739 — `pdp/gallery`  ❌ *design componentisation pending*

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-063, PRD-065*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/gallery` React component built to the Zimmermann Design
> System 2026 spec, so that it can be triggered from `pdp/carousel` to render a full-screen product
> image gallery overlay on the PDP.
>
> The component renders a full-screen overlay containing a sticky `pdp/gallery-header` and a
> scrollable vertical stack of `pdp/carousel/item` instances. It is triggered by the View Gallery
> button in `pdp/carousel` and manages its own open/close state. It does not own the carousel or
> product content — it receives the product media array as a prop and renders it within the gallery
> layout.

**Acceptance criteria**

### SFCC-648 — `pdp/size-selector`

*Labels: PRD-012, PRD-014, PRD-016, `pdp/size-selector`*
*Blocks: SFCC-92, SFCC-150 · Relates: SFCC-650*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/size-selector` React component built to the Zimmermann
> design system spec, so that it can be consumed by PDP and any other page-level stories that require
> size selection.
>
> The component should be built as a standalone PWA Kit React component, sourced from the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 Figma file. It renders a size selector UI displaying available sizes with their
> stock status. It does not handle inventory API integration — stock status is passed in as props.
> For one-size products, the standard selector UI is suppressed and replaced with a plain "One size"
> label.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Rendered with a list of sizes, no size selected → selector displays default state with placeholder label.
2. Shopper selects a size → selector displays filled state showing the selected size.
3. Selector in focus/open → renders active state showing all size options.
4. Size with stock status *in stock* → displays as standard selectable option.
5. Size with stock status *low stock* → displays with low availability indicator per design spec (PRD-012).
6. Size with stock status *out of stock* → renders as non-selectable, visually disabled option (PRD-014).
7. Size with stock status *notify me* → renders with Notify Me label per design spec (PRD-016); the Notify Me interaction itself handled by a separate story.
8. Size with status *recommended* → displays with a recommended indicator per design spec.
9. No valid size selected and selector in error state (triggered externally, e.g. by Add to Bag) → error state renders per design.
10. Rendered on mobile → renders using the mobile variant per design system spec.
11. Product has only one size → standard size selector UI not displayed; plain "One size" text label rendered in its place per approved PDP designs (PDP Low availability frame, file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs`).
12. Product has only one size → size automatically considered selected; no shopper interaction required to enable Add to Bag.

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
13. Keyboard user tabs to selector → visible focus ring per design system spec.
14. Arrow Up / Arrow Down → focus moves between size options without a mouse.
15. Enter or Space on a focused size option → that size is selected.
16. Error state triggered → focus retained on or moved to the selector so the user is aware.
17. Screen reader on a size option with a stock status indicator → stock status included in the accessible label, e.g. "Size 1 (US 6), Low Availability".
18. Error state with message → announced via ARIA live region without navigation.
19. Out-of-stock, non-selectable size option → announced as unavailable rather than skipped or only visually greyed.
20. One-size product with "One size" label → announced correctly as the selected size.
21. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum.

**Observations**
- **SFCC-150 describes this control as a dropdown** — "the standard size selector is displayed … and **in the dropdown**, with a 'Notify Me' CTA per individual size row." AC#1–3 (placeholder → filled → active/open) are consistent with a dropdown; AC#14's Arrow Up/Down model is a listbox pattern.
- **SFCC-150 also specifies a contextual placeholder string** — "Select size to get notified" for Coming Soon / Back in Soon / Unavailable states. AC#1 refers to "a placeholder label" without variants.
- AC#8's *recommended* status originates from Measmerize per **SFCC-101**: "Once Measmerize has generated a size recommendation … the shopper can click on Continue and that size will be selected in the PDP." SFCC-101 is not linked to this story.
- AC#7's *notify me* status triggers **SFCC-741**; SFCC-741 is not linked to this story (it links to SFCC-149 instead).
- 21 ACs total, of which 9 (#13–21) are accessibility.
- Blocks SFCC-92 (Blocked, 5 pts) and SFCC-150 (Ready For Review).
- Accessibility target stated as WCAG 2.1 AA.

### SFCC-650 — `pdp/add-to-bag`

*Labels: PRD-018*
*Blocks: SFCC-92, SFCC-150 · Relates: SFCC-648, SFCC-196*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/add-to-bag` React component built for the Zimmermann PWA
> Kit, so that it can be consumed by the PDP and any other page-level stories that require
> add-to-bag functionality.
>
> The component renders using the base Button component (Primary, Large) from the Zimmermann design
> system. It wraps it with add-to-bag-specific interaction logic: size selection validation, stock
> state awareness, loading state during cart API call, and inline error messaging. **Cart API
> integration is in scope for this story.** Maximum purchase quantity enforcement is handled
> separately in SFCC-196.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. No size selected on page load → Add to Bag CTA displayed but **disabled**.
2. Click Add to Bag without selecting a size → button remains inactive and "Size required" inline message displayed.
3. Select an in-stock size → Add to Bag CTA becomes active and enabled.
4. Click Add to Bag with valid size → cart API call made, button displays loading state while in flight.
5. Cart API call succeeds → item confirmed as added to bag and appropriate success state shown.
6. Cart API call fails → inline error message displayed, CTA returns to enabled state so shopper can retry.
7. One-size product → size treated as pre-selected, Add to Bag CTA active on page load.
8. Component accepts size selection state and stock status as props — does not manage size selection itself; that is owned by `pdp/size-selector` (SFCC-648).

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
9. Keyboard user tabs to CTA → visible focus ring per design system spec.
10. CTA in disabled state → announced as unavailable to screen reader users.
11. Inline error or success message → announced via ARIA live region without navigation.
12. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum.

**Observations**
- The description states "Cart API integration is in scope". The base template's `product-view/index.jsx` already performs `addToCart` / `updateCart`, uses `useAddToCartModalContext`, and raises a toast on success.
- AC#1 states the CTA is **disabled**; AC#2 states a click on it produces a "Size required" message; AC#10 states it is announced as unavailable. A natively `disabled` button cannot receive click or focus events.
- AC#5 refers to "the appropriate success state" without defining it. The base provides an add-to-cart modal and a toast. **SFCC-98 (Add to Bag — Fly-to-Bag Animation)** exists and is not linked.
- **SFCC-150 states that in Coming Soon / Back in Soon / Unavailable states "Add to Bag is suppressed"** and the CTA area displays a state label instead. No AC here covers a suppressed/replaced CTA. SFCC-650 is blocked by SFCC-150.
- Maximum purchase quantity is excluded to SFCC-196 (Tech design, unpointed). Both would gate the same click; the order of checks is not specified in either.
- Basket state is required to evaluate SFCC-196; `use-current-basket` is Tier 1.
- Accessibility target stated as WCAG 2.1 AA.

### SFCC-723 — `pdp/hero`

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-062, PRD-063, PRD-064, PRD-065, `pdp/hero`*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/hero` React component built to the Zimmermann Design System
> 2026 spec, so that it can be used as the top-level orchestration component for the PDP, composing
> the product image gallery and `pdp/product-content` into a single, responsive hero layout.
>
> The component is responsible for layout and composition only — it does not own the interaction
> logic of its child components. It accepts child components as composed instances (e.g. carousel,
> `pdp/product-content`, colour picker, size selector, add-to-bag, drawer triggers) and manages their
> arrangement across desktop and mobile breakpoints. The sole configuration prop is
> `showGalleryButton` (boolean), which controls whether the "View Gallery" CTA button overlay appears
> on the image gallery.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Layout — Desktop*
1. Desktop breakpoint: image gallery left, `pdp/product-content` right, spacing/proportions per design system.
2. Desktop gallery displays carousel items in sequence: single full-width images, and a 4-up 2x2 grid with a View Gallery button overlay on the bottom-right image.
3. Desktop carousel with a video item: video control icons (mute, play/pause) visible bottom-right of that item.

*Layout — Mobile*
4. Mobile breakpoint: gallery full-width top, `pdp/product-content` below in stacked column with padding per design system.
5. Mobile: dot-indicator carousel bar visible bottom-left, showing current position across available images.

*showGalleryButton prop*
6. `showGalleryButton` true → View Gallery button overlay visible.
7. `showGalleryButton` false → no View Gallery button overlay.

*Child component composition*
8. Does not replicate or override child interaction logic — size validation, add-to-bag API calls, drawer open/close, colour swatch selection are owned by their respective child stories.

*Responsiveness*
9. Viewport transitions between mobile and desktop switch layout between stacked and side-by-side with no layout breakage.

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
10. Keyboard focus order follows visual reading order: gallery first on desktop (left), product content second (right); stacked top-to-bottom on mobile.
11. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum; child component accessibility covered in their stories.

**Observations**
- AC#2 (desktop gallery layout), AC#5 (mobile dot indicator) and AC#6–7 (`showGalleryButton`) specify behaviour that is **also specified in SFCC-731** (`pdp/carousel` AC#1–5, 7–8, 9–11). The same behaviour is described in two tickets.
- AC#3 covers video control icons. **SFCC-186 states video content in the gallery is out of scope (SFCC-188).**
- The description states the component owns "layout and composition only", while AC#2, #3 and #5 describe carousel internals.
- No Jira links; all children referenced in prose only.
- Accessibility target stated as WCAG 2.1 AA.

---

### SFCC-737 — `pdp/product-content`

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/product-content` React component built to the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/hero` to render the full product
> information panel on the PDP.
>
> The component is a composition container. It does not own the logic of its child components —
> interaction behaviour for colour selection, size selection, add to bag, wishlist, and drawer
> triggers are covered in their respective child component stories. This story covers the layout,
> ordering, and rendering of all child elements within the panel, and the static content elements
> (product name, description, model description, style code) that are not extracted into separate
> components.

**Acceptance criteria**

*Composition & layout*
1. Renders elements top to bottom per design system: product name + wishlist icon, price, product description, `pdp/product-colour-picker`, `pdp/size-selector`, `pdp/add-to-bag`, Find in Boutique link, drawer trigger rows (Details & Care, Size & Fit, Shipping & Returns, Assistance), model description, style code.
2. Desktop layout and spacing match design system spec.
3. Mobile layout and spacing match mobile design system spec.

*Static content*
4. Product name displays in uppercase using heading typography style.
5. Product description displays below the price in body typography style.
6. Model description displays below drawer triggers in caption typography style.
7. Style code displays at bottom of panel in subtle text colour.

*Empty & error states*
9. No product description → element does not render, no empty space left.
10. No model description → element does not render.
11. No style code → element does not render.

### SFCC-731 — `pdp/carousel`

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-061, PRD-063, PRD-064, PRD-065, PRD-066*
*Blocks: SFCC-186 (PDP – Product Image Gallery)*

> ⚠️ **The Acceptance Criteria field is empty on this ticket.** The ACs below live in the
> description, and the numbering is mangled by Jira auto-numbering (all rendered as "1."). Some
> layout separators also appear to have been stripped (e.g. "2 full-width  2-up grid" likely means
> "2 full-width + 2-up grid").

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/carousel` React component built to the Zimmermann Design
> System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/hero` to render the product image and video
> gallery on the PDP.

> and a swipeable carousel on mobile. The desktop layout adapts based on total media count. Video is

> media array. The component renders a View Gallery button as a trigger only — the gallery overlay is
> a separate component and out of scope for this story.

**Acceptance criteria (as written in the description)**

*Desktop layout — media count thresholds*
1. 3 media items → 3 full-width stacked + View Gallery button
2. 4 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery button
3. 5 media items → 2 full-width + 2-up grid + View Gallery **1** button
4. 6 media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery button
5. 7 media items → 2 full-width + 4-up grid + View Gallery **X** button (X = total minus 6)
6. Video items slot into layout based on position in the media array — not treated differently to photos for layout purposes.

*showGalleryButton prop*
7. `showGalleryButton` false → no View Gallery button regardless of media count.
8. `showGalleryButton` true → View Gallery button renders per thresholds above, visible and tappable — overlay behaviour out of scope.

*Mobile*
9. Mobile: all media items display in a swipeable single-image carousel with dot indicator bar regardless of media count.
10. Swipe → active dot indicator updates to reflect current position.
11. `showGalleryButton` true on mobile → View Gallery button visible and tappable.

*Empty & error states*
12. No media items → component does not render, no broken layout.
13. Image fails to load → surrounding layout maintained without a broken image rendering — fallback behaviour TBD, see open items.

*Accessibility*
14. Carousel fully keyboard navigable and meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

**Open items (in ticket)**
- @Kiera — confirm media count threshold logic is correct per design specs shared.
- @Kiera — confirm fallback behaviour when an image fails to load (blank space, grey box, or branded fallback image).

- AC#6 places video items in scope. **SFCC-186, which this story blocks, states video content in the gallery is out of scope (SFCC-188).**
- SFCC-186 describes the desktop layout as "large hero followed by another large image, then supporting images in a 2x2 grid" and contains no media-count thresholds.
- Layout and `showGalleryButton` behaviour is also specified in SFCC-723 AC#2, #5, #6–7.

### SFCC-739 — `pdp/gallery`  ❌ *design componentisation pending*

*Labels: PRD-058, PRD-059, PRD-063, PRD-065*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/gallery` React component built to the Zimmermann Design

**Acceptance criteria**

*Overlay shell*
1. View Gallery button clicked in `pdp/carousel` → gallery opens full-screen, taking over entire viewport.
2. Gallery open → clicking close icon dismisses overlay and returns shopper to previous scroll position on the PDP.

*`pdp/gallery-header` — Desktop*

### SFCC-734 — `pdp/product-colour-picker`

*Labels: PRD-069*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/product-colour-picker` React component built to the
> Zimmermann Design System 2026 spec, so that it can be consumed by `pdp/product-content` to render
> the colour swatch selector on the PDP.
>
> The component renders a row of colour swatches, a "Colour:" label, and the name of the currently
> selected colour. Each swatch displays a cropped product image thumbnail. The component manages
> selected and unselected swatch states. It does not own the cross-component interactions triggered

**Acceptance criteria**

*Rendering*
1. "Colour:" label and active colour name display above the swatch row.
2. Each swatch displays a product image thumbnail at equal width.
3. Selected swatch renders with a visible bottom border indicator per design system.
4. Unselected swatch renders without the border indicator.

*Interaction*
5. Click a swatch → that swatch becomes selected and the colour name label updates.
6. Click an already-selected swatch → no state change.

*Empty & error states*
7. Only one colour variant → no swatch row renders; only "Colour:" label and colour name displayed.
8. Swatch image fails to load → swatch slot maintains dimensions without breaking layout.

*Accessibility*
9. Each swatch focusable and selectable via keyboard.

### SFCC-648 — `pdp/size-selector`

*Labels: PRD-012, PRD-014, PRD-016, `pdp/size-selector`*
*Blocks: SFCC-92, SFCC-150 · Relates: SFCC-650*

**Description**

> As a Developer, I want a reusable `pdp/size-selector` React component built to the Zimmermann
> design system spec, so that it can be consumed by PDP and any other page-level stories that require
> size selection.
>
> The component should be built as a standalone PWA Kit React component, sourced from the Zimmermann
> Design System 2026 Figma file. It renders a size selector UI displaying available sizes with their
> stock status. It does not handle inventory API integration — stock status is passed in as props.
> For one-size products, the standard selector UI is suppressed and replaced with a plain "One size"
> label.

**Acceptance criteria**

1. Rendered with a list of sizes, no size selected → selector displays default state with placeholder label.
2. Shopper selects a size → selector displays filled state showing the selected size.
3. Selector in focus/open → renders active state showing all size options.
4. Size with stock status *in stock* → displays as standard selectable option.
5. Size with stock status *low stock* → displays with low availability indicator per design spec (PRD-012).
6. Size with stock status *out of stock* → renders as non-selectable, visually disabled option (PRD-014).
7. Size with stock status *notify me* → renders with Notify Me label per design spec (PRD-016); the Notify Me interaction itself handled by a separate story.
8. Size with status *recommended* → displays with a recommended indicator per design spec.
9. No valid size selected and selector in error state (triggered externally, e.g. by Add to Bag) → error state renders per design.
10. Rendered on mobile → renders using the mobile variant per design system spec.
11. Product has only one size → standard size selector UI not displayed; plain "One size" text label rendered in its place per approved PDP designs (PDP Low availability frame, file `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs`).
12. Product has only one size → size automatically considered selected; no shopper interaction required to enable Add to Bag.

*Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)*
13. Keyboard user tabs to selector → visible focus ring per design system spec.
14. Arrow Up / Arrow Down → focus moves between size options without a mouse.
15. Enter or Space on a focused size option → that size is selected.
16. Error state triggered → focus retained on or moved to the selector so the user is aware.
17. Screen reader on a size option with a stock status indicator → stock status included in the accessible label, e.g. "Size 1 (US 6), Low Availability".
18. Error state with message → announced via ARIA live region without navigation.
19. Out-of-stock, non-selectable size option → announced as unavailable rather than skipped or only visually greyed.
20. One-size product with "One size" label → announced correctly as the selected size.
21. Meets WCAG 2.1 AA as minimum.

**Observations**
- **SFCC-150 describes this control as a dropdown** — "the standard size selector is displayed … and **in the dropdown**, with a 'Notify Me' CTA per individual size row." AC#1–3 (placeholder → filled → active/open) are consistent with a dropdown; AC#14's Arrow Up/Down model is a listbox pattern.
- **SFCC-150 also specifies a contextual placeholder string** — "Select size to get notified" for Coming Soon / Back in Soon / Unavailable states. AC#1 refers to "a placeholder label" without variants.
- AC#8's *recommended* status originates from Measmerize per **SFCC-101**: "Once Measmerize has generated a size recommendation … the shopper can click on Continue and that size will be selected in the PDP." SFCC-101 is not linked to this story.
- AC#7's *notify me* status triggers **SFCC-741**; SFCC-741 is not linked to this story (it links to SFCC-149 instead).
- 21 ACs total, of which 9 (#13–21) are accessibility.
- Blocks SFCC-92 (Blocked, 5 pts) and SFCC-150 (Ready For Review).
- Accessibility target stated as WCAG 2.1 AA.
